articles.title: There was little fuss about data centers in the last election. Now they could sway the midterms.
articles.summary: AI data centers have become a key issue in the 2026 midterms.
articles.body:
Opposition to data centers, an issue barely on anyone's radar in the 2024 election, has now united voters across the political spectrum .

According to a May Gallup poll , more than 70% of Americans are opposed to AI data center construction in their local area. It makes sense when you consider that this midterms cycle is heavily focused on rising living costs . Data centers — facilities that store, process and distribute digital data, and have become more common in the AI era — use up massive amounts of water and electricity, raising concerns that the costs will be passed down to local communities in the form of electric bill hikes and water rate increases.

The Data Center Opposition Project , which tracks the rise of grassroots nonprofits in the U.S. that are against the development of data centers, recently found that more than 200 new groups popped up between June and August of this year, suggesting the issue has salience with voters across the country.

Heading into the midterms, that could be a major problem for candidates and incumbents who have supported data center projects. And in many cases, their opponents are making sure voters are well aware of their positions.

President Trump has strongly supported data centers. He views them as key to winning the AI race against China, but also for economic growth and the creation of local jobs. "If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign," he wrote in an August Truth Social post. On the flip side, progressives like Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Sen. Bernie Sanders have proposed a national moratorium on new AI data centers "until strong national safeguards are in place."

Ohio will soon be home to what the Trump administration calls the " world's largest AI data center. " SB Energy , a development company, will build and own the site, with OpenAI leasing it for 20 years. Nvidia announced a $1.5 billion investment in SB Energy as part of the deal. The PORTS-Pike Technology Campus , as the Ohio data center project is known, is slated to begin construction this year. And like many data centers, it's in a rural area near Piketon, a village of roughly 2,200 residents about 70 miles south of Columbus, where there is ample space for the sprawling facility.

Residents there have mixed feelings about the project. Some are being offered significant sums of money for their properties, which may mean a piece of land that's been in their family for generations. Samantha McCaughey, a barista at the Village Brew Coffee House in Piketon, told Yahoo that her grandfather is weighing a six-figure offer for the family's nearly 100-acre property near the data center site.

"They've lived there their whole life, so it's really difficult for them," McCaughey said. "They're still kind of on the fence, but I mean, with everything going on, is it worth even staying if everything is changing?"

In June, a citizen-led effort to put a statewide data center ban on the November ballot fell short . However, 18 communities in Ohio will have data center measures on their local ballots this year. Half of the petitions ask voters to decide whether to ban any centers that draw more than 25 megawatts of energy from the local grid per month. And there are more than 100 moratoriums on new data centers in communities across the state. An August poll from Bowling Green State University found 78% of Ohioans support these temporary moratoriums.

Ohio ranks fourth among states with the most operational data centers, and the issue has been a centerpiece of former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown's ad campaign against incumbent Republican Sen. Jon Husted. An AdImpact analysis of spending on campaign ads this cycle found Democrats far outspent Republicans on data center-themed ads, with most of them either attacking the centers or linking a candidate to the center's potential negative impacts. Brown's campaign spent $2.4 million on data center-themed ads. Those included attacks on Husted for his past support of data centers, repeating the label given to him as "the face of data centers in Ohio." In recent months, however, Husted has worked to put guardrails on them.

"They're devouring our farmland, sucking up our water, and using our energy," Brown says in one ad , where he accuses Husted of giving huge tax breaks to companies like Meta, which is building a 715,000-square-foot data center in northwest Ohio. "I'm fighting to give you a voice to make sure these data centers don't flood our communities and raise our electric rates."

And indeed, the water and electricity-guzzling facilities are needed to power artificial intelligence. According to a 2025 report from the International Energy Agency , the typical AI data center consumes as much electricity as 100,000 households every year. The agency predicts the largest data centers under construction will use 20 times that amount.

The facilities also consume vast amounts of water, in part because they need to cool their processor chips. According to the Environmental and Energy Study Institute , large data centers may use up to five million gallons of water per day. A Bloomberg analysis found that in areas with "significant data center activity," wholesale electricity prices rose as much as 267% from 2020 to 2025. Those costs are being passed along to utility customers.

Axios reported in August that an internal memo from the National Republican Senatorial Committee said strong opposition to data centers had become damaging to Husted's reelection bid. In addition, the race may be a warning signal for other candidates. "If [Husted] loses and data centers get the blame, politicians across the country will take notice — and they will not go near the next one," the memo says. "This has become a sleeper issue for the entire election cycle."

Recent polling averages show Brown leading Husted by around 3 percentage points and the nonpartisan Cook Political Report has rated the race as a toss up .

Husted's campaign secretary, Tom Evans, noted in an email to Yahoo that Husted had introduced the Senate companion bill to the Ratepayer Protection Act (RPA), which passed the U.S. House on Sept. 16 by a vote of 417-3. The RPA would require state utility regulators to consider adopting a federal standard under which large data centers would cover the extra costs of upgrades — potentially preventing those costs from getting passed along to other customers.

A vote on Husted's bill was blocked by Senate Democrats, who said it didn't go far enough. "Sherrod Brown and his friends would rather play politics and stick Ohio families with higher electric bills than pass a commonsense solution," Evans said to Yahoo, pointing to Brown's earlier support of a data center project in 2015.

While some Ohio communities have pushed back hard against new data centers, in Piketon, locals still seem uncertain.

"Residents have been asking good questions — hard questions — about data centers and we are asking good, hard questions too," Pike County Commissioner Tony Montgomery told Yahoo. "We have set no deadline on considering this project and have involved public officials throughout the county in our review."

McCaughey said she likes Piketon's "cozy" vibe and is a little wary of the coming growth, but that she sees the upside as well. "It's cool seeing how things are going to grow and how many people are going to have jobs that might otherwise have been struggling," she said.

Local officials say they expect an estimated 35,000 temporary construction jobs and 2,500 permanent jobs to be created. Meanwhile, data center operators argue that when one of them enters a community, other businesses, including tech companies, financial institutions and retail companies, usually follow.

Brown told Yahoo that local governments shouldn't offer tax breaks as incentives for developers to build data centers in their communities. "They're billionaires. They don't need tax breaks to come in," he said, adding that local residents should have a say in decisions about data center proposals. "Local communities have just been run over in this."

He added that local communities should make sure any agreements require data centers to pay for their own power usage.

When asked about rural landowners near data centers who are debating whether to sell or stay, Brown advised those who decide to sell to "make sure they drive a hard bargain, and that [the data centers] are responsible with the land."

Data centers take center stage in the midterms

Ohio isn't the only state where data centers have become a political issue — and Brown isn't the only candidate spotlighting his opponent's support for them in the midterms races.

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who is running for the Senate in Michigan, has criticized his Republican opponent Mike Rogers for his investments in companies tied to data centers (the sound of a data center is all you hear in one of El-Sayed's campaign ads). In August, Rogers called for a one-year moratorium on new data center development. Meanwhile, officials in Wayne County, which includes Detroit, recently voted to advance a proposed 1.5 million-square-foot Google data center.

In Florida, which ranks 12th among the states with the most data centers currently operating or planned, Democrat David Jolly and Republican Byron Donalds have both run ads on the issue in the gubernatorial race. Jolly has called for a moratorium and criticizes Donalds for receiving donations from AI and data center companies . Donalds has called for companies building the data centers to absorb their costs.

This is an idea that continues to gain traction even among those who support data center construction.

On Wednesday, Trump posted on Truth Social that he had " come to a very strong conclusion " — that new and large data centers should "make their own electricity, and give or sell excess back to the local community, or grid" if companies want to make them popular. The comment signals how prominent the issue has become for voters.

Some candidates have been hearing more from constituents concerned about proposed projects as they meet face-to-face. At a town hall in his southwestern Pennsylvania district on Oct. 17, Rep. Chris Deluzio said communities should have a voice in decisions related to data centers.

"I don't think you should get steamrolled by these corporations," Deluzio said. "There's a lot of money in this industry. I don't think they need our public money."

Governors in some states that welcomed data centers have recently pumped the brakes in response to the public backlash. Gov. Josh Shapiro of Pennsylvania signed an executive order in August tightening permitting requirements for large data centers. The order requires local approval before certain new projects can receive state permits, and removes existing projects from the state's fast-tracked permitting process. That provision applies to a $20 billion commitment Amazon made last year to build multiple AI data centers across the state, which Shapiro embraced at the time.

And in Virginia — a state whose northern region has become known as Data Center Alley — Gov. Abigail Spanberger presented a set of legislative proposals that would curb data center development. Her "Data Center Accountability Framework" stops short of a statewide moratorium, but includes plans to lower energy costs, promote clean energy and put environmental protections in place. It would also bar non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) between local governments and data center developers. Many argue NDAs prevent residents from learning details of data center proposals until late in the process.

NDAs have been used in data center projects across Virginia, researchers at the University of Mary Washington found. And Virginia has had data centers long before the facilities became associated with AI. In 1998, two years after AOL moved into Loudoun County , Va., Equinix built the region's first data center partly to help store the internet service provider's data. Amazon built its first data center in Loudoun in 2006.

According to the county's website , Loudoun boasts "the highest concentration of data centers anywhere in the world." In fiscal year 2026, its data centers brought in $1.2 billion in property tax revenue, it says. That number is projected to climb to $1.3 billion, or 40% of the county's overall budget, in 2027.

With the midterms looming, an October New York Times/Siena University poll found that while data centers are not the top issue for most Ohio voters, it's a bigger midterm issue there than in four other states — Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — that were surveyed. Most Ohio voters are opposed to new data center construction, and more of them said they trusted Brown to handle the issue over Husted.

For her part, McCaughey said her family is accustomed to living in a rural area, and she doesn't want to see that go away. "My dad loves going out and hunting and just being in the woods," she said. "Knowing that it would be lost is really sad."

articles.title: Isofix: O que é e como usar para transporte infantil seguro | G1
articles.standfirst: O Isofix é a melhor e mais segura forma para transportar uma criança pequena no veículo de passeio; veja como garantir a instalação segura, segundo as regras do Contran.
articles.summary: Entenda o que é Isofix, sistema mais seguro para transportar crianças no carro. Veja como garantir a instalação correta, conforme as regras do Contran, e evite erros.
articles.body:
Pontos de ancoragem do Isofix em um Volkswagen Golf — Foto: divulgação/Volkswagen

A escolha e o uso adequado da cadeirinha infantil ainda despertam dúvidas entre pais e responsáveis, mesmo após a sua obrigatoriedade em veículos de passeio, estabelecida em setembro de 2010.

Uma das formas de prender o bebê conforto, cadeirinha ou assento de elevação nos carros é o Isofix, que ancora a cadeirinha ao assento traseiro do carro. Porém, a lei do Isofix foi sancionada em 2015 e somente em 2020 é que passou a ser obrigatória para todos os veículos novos fabricados ou importados no país.

Este tipo de ancoragem exige pontos de fixação específicos, tanto no veículo quanto na cadeirinha.

O sistema é composto por dois pontos de fixação na base da cadeirinha ou do bebê-conforto, que se encaixam a dois pontos no veículo, localizados no vão entre o assento e o encosto do banco traseiro.

Localizar os pontos de ancoragem no banco traseiro , que podem ser visíveis como na imagem acima, ou escondidos. Neste caso, um ícone de cadeirinha infantil ou o nome "Isofix" fica visível.

Guiar os pontos da cadeirinha aos locais do banco e empurrar , até escutar um "clique".

Em algumas cadeirinhas, uma indicação em verde aparece próxima do local de ancoragem no assento do veículo.

Ponto de ancoragem Isofix em um Volkswagen Golf — Foto: divulgação/Volkswagen

Um terceiro ponto pode estar no carro e ele se liga a uma espécie de gancho da cadeirinha, evitando que o dispositivo se movimente. Esse ponto tem nome de Top Tether e, se estiver no seu carro, estará em um dos seguintes locais:

Na parte de trás do encosto (na área do porta-malas, como na imagem abaixo);

Na lateral do carro (na mesma área de onde saem os cintos de segurança).

Top tether em um Volvo XC40 — Foto: divulgação/Volvo

Bebê conforto, cadeirinha e assento com elevação: os dispositivos indispensáveis para transportar crianças — Foto: g1

Confira abaixo as principais dúvidas sobre transporte seguro de crianças em carros:

Como usar e fixar o assento de elevação?

Quando a criança pode ir no banco da frente?

No papel, a regra do Conselho Nacional de Trânsito (Contran) define faixas etárias para cada tipo de equipamento:

Cadeirinha: de 1 a 4 anos ou entre 9 kg e 18 kg;

Assento de elevação: de 4 a 7 anos; entre 15 kg e 36 kg ou até 1,45 m de altura;

Banco traseiro com cinto de segurança: de 7 anos a 10 anos, desde que a criança tenha pelo menos 1,45 m de altura.

O uso incorreto da cadeirinha, além da insegurança para o bebê ou a criança, inclui multa de R$ 293,47, sete pontos na CNH e retenção do veículo.

O Inmetro, que certifica os produtos, classifica os dispositivos por grupos que combinam idade, peso e altura. Há modelos que abrangem mais de um grupo e podem ser usados por mais tempo.

“Existem cadeirinhas certificadas que comportam de 0 kg a 25 kg, por exemplo. Outras duram praticamente todo o tempo em que a criança vai precisar usar dispositivo de retenção”, explica Gustavo Kuster, do Inmetro.

O modelo da cadeirinha deve acompanhar o crescimento da criança, garantindo que ela esteja sempre firme e protegida. Como cada versão é indicada para uma faixa etária específica, a troca do equipamento se torna necessária conforme o desenvolvimento.

A transição entre os dispositivos deve considerar, na seguinte ordem de prioridade:

Um bebê que já não cabe no bebê conforto, por exemplo, pode ir para a cadeirinha, mesmo que ainda não tenha completado a idade mínima para a transição.

“Se ela ainda cabe naquele dispositivo, está confortável, com o cinto bem preso, pode continuar nele”, afirma Kuster.

A posição do bebê conforto — voltado para o encosto do banco — é recomendada por causa da anatomia dos recém-nascidos. “O bebê nasce com a cabeça maior que o corpo, como na forma de um martelo. Nessa posição, ele fica mais protegido”, explica Celso Arruda, especialista da Unicamp.

Para os mais crescidos, a altura é o fator mais importante na hora de dispensar o assento de elevação.

Crianças com menos de 1,45 m não devem usar apenas o cinto de segurança, mesmo que tenham mais de 7 anos. O assento serve para posicionar corretamente o cinto de três pontos, que deve passar pelo peito.

“Se ela ainda não tiver altura suficiente e quiser continuar usando inclusive a cadeirinha completa, sem dispensar o encosto, ainda que tenha mais de 4 anos ou mais de 36 kg, tudo bem. Desde que esteja confortável”, afirma Kuster.

O lugar mais seguro para transportar a criança é o banco traseiro, com cinto de três pontos e o dispositivo adequado. Mas há exceções.

Em carros que só têm cinto de dois pontos no banco de trás — e não há cadeirinha certificada para esse tipo de cinto — o ideal é levar a criança no banco da frente, com cinto de três pontos e o equipamento de retenção.

Mas é preciso desligar o airbag, nos carros equipados com o dispositivo e a depender da posição, para não eclodir em caso de acidente e causar mais danos do que proteger a criança.

“Dar um jeito de fixar a cadeirinha feita para cinto de três pontos em um cinto com dois pontos é ruim”, alerta Fábio Viviani, especialista em segurança veicular.

“Pode até parecer que ficou firme, mas nos crash tests é impressionante ver as forças envolvidas. A cadeirinha sem esse terceiro ponto de fixação não vai trabalhar da maneira como foi projetada”.

Nesses casos, a recomendação é recuar o banco dianteiro ao máximo, para afastar a criança do painel.

O Contran permite o transporte no banco da frente em situações específicas:

Crianças a partir de 10 anos, com cinto de segurança;

Quando o banco traseiro só tem cinto de dois pontos;

Em veículos sem banco traseiro, como picapes de cabine simples;

Quando há mais crianças do que lugares no banco traseiro — a de maior estatura pode ir na frente;

Segundo a Senatran, apenas bebê conforto, cadeirinha e assento de elevação são considerados dispositivos adequados. O Inmetro reforça que não há certificação para outros tipos de equipamentos.

“Sem um equipamento certificado, ou seja, que passou por testes rigorosos, a criança não estará devidamente protegida”, afirma Viviani.

articles.title: Race to Dubai: Can Eugenio Chacarra hold off Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy in DP World Tour play-offs to take No 1 spot?
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy heads into the DP World Tour play-offs trailing Eugenio Chacarra and Patrick Reed in the Order of Merit; McIlroy looks to win the Race to Dubai for a record-equalling eighth time; watch the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship live on Sky Sports Golf from Thursday
articles.body:
The DP World Tour campaign reaches its climax over the next fortnight in the Middle East, live on Sky Sports , with the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship beginning on Thursday ahead of next week's DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.

Seve Ballesteros and Jon Rahm are the only previous Spaniards to end the season as European No 1 and lift the Harry Vardon Trophy, with Chacarra in a strong position to join that major-winning duo after an impressive season.

Chacarra won the KLM Open and the DS Automobiles 83° Open d'Italia in June before adding a third victory of the year at last month's DP World India Championship, pulling him clear of Reed and McIlroy at the top of the standings.

"To be leading the Race to Dubai with two events to go is a dream," said Chacarra, who has four additional top-three finishes on the DP World Tour this season - including a second on home soil at the Open de Espana.

"To have the chance to win the Harry Vardon Trophy would be very special. I know the players behind me will push hard in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, but I'm playing the best golf of my career and I can't wait to get there."

On the challenge of staying No 1, Chacarra added: "They [Reed and McIlroy] are two of the best players in the world and we know what's Rory's record in Dubai. I need to play as good as possible the next couple of weeks.

"Hopefully I can keep playing good, keep doing good, and I can put my name with Jon's [Rahm] and Seve's [Ballesteros], that would be a dream come true."

The winner in Abu Dhabi claims 1,500 Race to Dubai points and the champion the following week earns 2,000, with Chacarra taking a 669.27-point lead over Reed and 999.03-point advantage over McIlroy heading into the DP World Tour Play-Offs.

Players are awarded a share of the points based on their finishing position, with Reed needing a share of second or better in Abu Dhabi to have any chance of reclaiming top spot from Chacarra before the DP World Tour Championship.

McIlroy remains in the hunt to claim a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title and fourth in as many years, but The Masters champion will need a big finish to the season to finish No 1 and match Colin Montgomerie's record of Order of Merit titles.

"Eugenio [Chacarra] is playing well - that makes my job a bit harder going into the last two events," McIlroy admitted after a tied-42nd finish in India last month.

South Africa's Casey Jarvis sits fourth in the standings and is 1,287.81 points behind Chacarra, while PGA champion Aaron Rai - the defending champion in Abu Dhabi - rounds off the top five.

Strong line-up despite Middle East uncertainty

Only the top 70 available golfers in the Race to Dubai standings can feature in the Abu Dhabi, before dropping to the top 50 the following week, although multiple eligible players have elected against tee it up in the opening play-off.

Several of those not involved have previously expressly safety concerns about playing in the Middle East, given fears of a wider regional conflict, with Matt Fitzpatrick, Bob MacIntyre and Shane Lowry among those sitting out in Abu Dhabi.

On the possibility of disruption, a DP World Tour spokesperson told Sky Sports last week: "The Foreign Office has not issued advice against travel to the UAE so our situation remains the same.

"We intend staging our play-off events as scheduled in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, but we remain in contact with our international advisors."

All of the top five in the Race to Dubai standings will feature in Abu Dhabi, along with past champions Tommy Fleetwood and Tyrrell Hatton, while former world No 1s Rahm and Adam Scott are also still listed in the field.

Open champion Ryan Fox - sixth in the standings - is the highest-ranked player not playing in Abu Dhabi, although the New Zealander is currently still scheduled to feature at the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.

What else is up for grabs and how can I watch?

Chacarra and Reed have already secured their PGA Tour cards for next season via the Race to Dubai rankings, awarded to the leading 10 players not already exempt in the standings.

Jarvis, Daniel Hillier, Jayden Schaper and Jacob Skov Olesen are among those currently inside those projected spots, with English duo Andy Sullivan and Joe Dean also challenging for PGA Tour cards.

The next two events also decides the Sir Henry Cotton Rookie of the Year Award, awarded to the highest-ranked player in their maiden DP World Tour season, with Japan's Kota Kaneko currently leading South Africa's Michael Hollick in that race.

Sky Sports will show live coverage from all four rounds at Yas Links GC, with the action live from 7am on Sky Sports Golf on each of the first three days and then getting under way at 6.30am on Sunday.

Who will win the Race to Dubai? Watch the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship and the DP World Tour Championship live on Sky Sports. Get the latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract .

articles.title: Man caught in car with £14k of drugs as a lamb ate chips in the back seat avoids jail
articles.summary: Police officers found the animal in the back seat of John McNeil's car on the M74 in Glasgow.
articles.body:
A man who was caught in a car with £14,000 of drugs, while a lamb ate from a bag of chips in the back seat, has avoided jail.

John McNeil, 56, was a passenger in Lindsey Sangster's vehicle which was stopped by police on the M74 in Glasgow on 22 April 2023.

Bags of heroin and cocaine were later recovered by a police dog underneath the front passenger seat of the Volkswagen Golf.

When quizzed about the animal - called Pablo - a sergeant claimed Sangster's partner McNeil told him she was a "trainee shepherdess." The duo were found guilty in September of possession of cocaine and diamorphine with intent to supply.

The pair claimed they had tried to save the lamb - named after Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar - from a "dangerous position" on the middle of the road.

The court previously heard Pablo belonged to North Lanrigg Farm in Motherwell, which is owned by farmer Kirsty Mair.

A joint minute of agreed evidence said Mair had not given them permission to have the lamb.

Sgt Nick Twigg, 42, told jurors that he had reason to stop Sangster's car on the motorway, with Sangster, McNeil and another man in the vehicle.

An initial search found a glass pipe in the driver's door pocket while others were seized from McNeil and the man.

He said: "I asked Sangster where it [the lamb] came from and McNeil said that she was a trainee shepherdess."

Prosecutor Julianna Keenan asked the officer if there was evidence of this and he replied: "No, the lamb at the time was eating a bag of chips left on the back seat. There were no bottles."

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

A police dog named Billy later found £4,640 of cocaine and £10,050 of heroin under the front passenger seat within two bags.

The purity of the cocaine was stated to be no less than 76%.

In a joint minute of agreed evidence, Keenan said: "Officers were of the opinion that the circumstances of this case indicate the supply of cocaine and heroin due to the amount recovered being excessive for personal use."

Pablo was taken to a farm in Ayrshire where it was held for 48 to 72 hours before being returned to Mair.

A charge of resetting the lamb was dropped by the Crown mid-trial as there was "no reported theft" at the time.

McNeil told jurors in his evidence that he had experience with animals, having worked in the past with his father, who is a retired agricultural contractor.

He stated they came across Pablo on the middle of the road on the way home to Ayrshire after a journey to Edinburgh for the other man to purchase a car.

McNeil claimed that Pablo was "dehydrated" and appeared not have been fed for a couple of hours.

He told the court that the plan was to "take him back to the owner" as Pablo had identity markings on his ears.

McNeil denied any knowledge of the drugs in the car, as did Sangster.

Jurors were told that Sangster was under the influence of drugs at the time when she was behind the wheel and pleaded guilty at separate proceedings.

She was disqualified from driving for 18 months and ordered to do 100 hours of unpaid work.

Bronwyn Moore, defending McNeil at the sentencing, said her client was now a team leader at a construction company and that he was "at the height of his addiction" when arrested.

McNeil, of Fairlie, North Ayrshire, was back in the dock to be sentenced while Sangster, of Kilbirnie, did not appear and a warrant was granted for her arrest.

Sheriff Tony Kelly ordered McNeil to do 300 hours of unpaid work and tagged him for six months, meaning he must stay indoors between 20:00 and 05:00.

The sheriff said he had been advised the risk of McNeil offending again was low.

After the lamb was returned to Mair, she said he was in fine health and happy with "his new pet lamb pals".

articles.title: Delhi records season’s first ‘very poor’ AQI at 324; GRAP-2 curbs imposed, border checks snarl traffic
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated to the ‘very poor’ category for the first time this season on Monday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI)
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated to the ‘very poor’ category for the first time this season on Monday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) settling at 324 by 4 pm, the highest level in nine months.As pollution levels worsened, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) invoked Stage 2 of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR, while intensified checks at the capital’s borders to enforce vehicle restrictions left commuters stuck in long traffic queues.The AQI of 324 was the highest recorded since February 4, when it stood at 339. The city’s pollution levels had risen sharply over the previous two days, from 117 in the ‘moderate’ category on October 31 to 261 in the ‘poor’ category on November 1, before entering the ‘very poor’ category on Monday.Three of Delhi’s air quality monitoring stations reported ‘severe’ pollution at 4pm. Jahangirpuri recorded the worst AQI at 436, followed by Rohini at 415 and Punjabi Bagh at 413.Of the city’s 58 monitoring stations, 37 reported ‘very poor’ air quality, 17 were in the ‘poor’ category and one recorded ‘moderate’ air quality.Fine particulate matter, or PM2.5, remained the dominant pollutant. These particles, measuring 2.5 micrometres or less, can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream.GRAP Stage 2 invoked across Delhi-NCRThe CAQM said Delhi’s AQI had risen sharply due to unfavourable meteorological conditions and was likely to remain in the ‘very poor’ category over the coming days, according to forecasts by the India Meteorological Department and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology.Stage 2 of GRAP applies when the AQI is between 301 and 400. The emergency measures are intended to prevent further deterioration in air quality.The AQI is expected to remain in the ‘very poor’ category from November 3 to 5, according to the Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi, before improving marginally to the ‘poor’ category over the subsequent six days.The Decision Support System for Delhi estimated that the transport sector contributed 19.2% to the city’s pollution on Monday.Industries in Delhi and peripheral areas accounted for 4.2%, while residential activities contributed 4.9%. Stubble burning accounted for 8.4% of the pollution, with other sources contributing 20.7%.Among neighbouring NCR districts, Jhajjar accounted for 6.9% of the pollution, followed by Sonipat at 5.1%, Gurgaon at 2.9%, Rohtak at 2.7%, Ghaziabad at 2.6%, Baghpat at 2.4%, and Panipat and Bhiwani at 2% each. Gautam Buddha Nagar accounted for 1.9%.Border checks leave commuters stuck for hoursThe second day of the restrictions on vehicles entering Delhi saw intensified checks at several interstate borders, triggering long traffic queues on roads connecting the capital with Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.Heavy congestion was reported at the Delhi-Gurgaon, Delhi-Noida, Delhi-Ghaziabad, Delhi-Sonipat and Delhi-Najafgarh borders. On NH-48, traffic remained backed up for several kilometres near the Sirhaul toll plaza, affecting both the main carriageway and service roads. Similar snarls were reported near Noida and Ghaziabad.At the Aya Nagar border, Delhi Traffic Police and Transport Department teams turned back vehicles that did not meet the prescribed BS-VI emission standards.Officials said checks were being conducted across borders under different traffic police ranges, with fines also being issued for violations and incomplete vehicle documents.The restrictions, effective from November 1 as part of the winter pollution-control measures, bar petrol and diesel vehicles registered outside Delhi that do not meet BS-VI emission standards from entering the capital. Electric and CNG vehicles, along with BS-VI-compliant vehicles, are exempt.The enforcement is being jointly carried out by the Delhi Environment and Transport Departments and the traffic police at several entry points, including Rajokri on NH-48, DND Flyway, Ghazipur, Singhu, Tikri and Badarpur.The Northern Range of Delhi Traffic Police said its teams checked 7,657 vehicles between midnight on November 1 and noon on November 2, turning back 609 vehicles that did not comply with the restrictions.The drive was aimed at enforcing GRAP-related vehicle curbs and preventing non-compliant vehicles from entering the capital.On November 1, Delhi Traffic Police had checked 7,279 vehicles between midnight and 8 pm, turned back 714 and impounded 38, according to an earlier statement.The department also held a coordination meeting with police officials from neighbouring districts and used information boards, pamphlets, print media, social media and radio to publicise the restrictions.Delhi environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa said enforcement teams had checked 14,930 vehicles on November 1, issued 566 challans for Pollution Under Control Certificate violations and inspected 300 construction sites.HC declines interim relief against vehicle restrictionsThe Delhi high court on Monday refused to stay the ban on the entry of non-Delhi-registered vehicles that do not meet BS-VI emission standards. The restrictions are in force from November 1 to January 31.A bench of acting chief justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and justice Sanjay Sharma issued notice on a petition filed by Faridabad-based lawyer Gurmukh Dass Kohli and listed it for hearing with a related matter on November 27.The petitioner challenged the June 23 notification issued by the Department of Environment and Forests, arguing that the restriction discriminates between vehicles based on where they are registered rather than their emission standards.The plea pointed out that pre-BS-VI vehicles registered in Delhi remain allowed to ply in the capital, while comparable vehicles registered in Haryana are barred.The petition also argued that the blanket restriction applies irrespective of the AQI on a given day and affects the movement of residents across the integrated National Capital Region. It questioned the scientific basis of the decision and contended that less restrictive measures could have been considered.SC allows certified green crackers for two daysIn a separate development, the Supreme Court allowed the sale of certified green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR from November 4 to 6 and their bursting between 6am and 7am and 8pm and 10pm on November 7 and 8. The complete ban on firecrackers will be restored from November 9.The bench of justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale imposed conditions to prevent conventional and unauthorised firecrackers from being sold as green crackers.Manufacturers must have valid CSIR-NEERI certification and PESO licences, while each box must carry a product- and batch-specific QR code.Firecrackers containing barium, those not approved by CSIR-NEERI and crackers joined in series, commonly known as ‘ladis’, have been prohibited.The court also directed authorities to designate specific sale locations, with online sales prohibited, and asked police teams to inspect markets, verify QR codes and confiscate illegal firecrackers.No firecrackers will be allowed within 300 metres of hospitals, healthcare centres, old-age homes, educational institutions and notified silence zones.In its October 29 order, the court said a complete ban was facilitating the illegal sale of conventional firecrackers while preventing people from buying legitimate green crackers tested at established facilities.It also flagged the lack of adequate data on whether the ban imposed in 2024 had served its purpose, particularly in the absence of a significant improvement in AQI readings.The bench directed the CPCB, in consultation with state pollution control boards, to prepare daily air quality reports for the pre-Diwali period, November 2 to 6, Diwali, November 7 and 8, and the post-Diwali period, November 9 to 30.Authorities have also been asked to monitor pollution levels, inspect non-functional AQI monitoring stations and ensure post-festival waste clearance.The court warned that contempt action could be taken against officials for failing to implement its directions.(With agency inputs)You Can articles.title: Labour to end power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row
articles.summary: Labour's ruling National Executive Committee sets out where it is cutting ties with the Greens.
articles.body:
The Labour Party has pulled out of power-sharing agreements with the Green Party in 11 local councils, after the national party adopted a policy defining Zionism as a form of racism.

Labour councillors will no longer be in coalition with the Greens in areas including Sheffield, Warwick and Lewes.

Labour Party chair Bridget Phillipson said: "Labour has been clear from the start that the "Zionism is Racism" policy crosses a line and we cannot work with any party that supports it – at any level of government."

The Green Party said it was "hugely disappointed" that Labour had forced local leaders into "jeopardising successful progressive partnerships that are delivering benefits for residents".

In a joint statement, the Green Party and the Local Government Association Green Group said "top-down directives to break up and disrupt locally-run services are not in the interests of the residents we represent.

"We trust local communities, local councillors and local leaders to know what is best for them. We ask that others do the same."

In October, Green Party members backed a motion, entitled "Zionism is racism", which said Zionism was an ideology that supported an "ethnonationalist Jewish State in historic Palestine". It also backed a "single democratic Palestinian State", including in modern-day Israel.

Having been backed by party members, the motion became Green Party policy, but it has left senior figures bitterly divided . Jewish groups and opposition political parties have condemned it.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham told MPs in October that Labour would not partner with the Greens over the "antisemitic" policy.

Labour then issued an ultimatum from Labour's head office to Labour-Green councils, demanding that local Greens disown the motion passed by members at their national party conference.

Green groups were also asked to call on their party's national leadership to reconsider the policy.

Labour said there were local agreements in place in 18 authorities. Of those, Labour said 11 had not met the criteria it demanded.

Lewes District Council (The Green Party announced last week it was "mutually" ending its alliance with Labour)

Runnymede Borough Council (Labour says local co-operation had already ceased)

Labour said its conditions had been met in Broadland, Monmouthshire, North Somerset, Rother, West Oxfordshire and West Sussex. The party said that Coventry City Council does not have a formal arrangement in place and that no such deal will be made in the future.

It will continue co-operating with the Greens in the West of England mayoralty, where the deputy mayor is a Green member.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski has said the motion was "imperfect" but has defended its central premise , arguing that Israel's actions towards the Palestinian people are "clearly underpinned by racist ideology".

The collapse of co-operation at the local level could impact hundreds of thousands of residents through budgets and policy decisions taking longer to get voted through.

Green and Labour councillors in the impacted areas will now have to seek alternative coalition partners or try to govern as a minority administration.

One of the biggest councils to be affected is Sheffield, where 25 Labour councillors formed a power-sharing agreement with 20 Green councillors after the May 2026 elections for the Yorkshire city's 550,000 residents.

Responding to Labour's ultimatum, leader of the Sheffield Greens Angela Argenzio did not mention the motion in a letter but insisted local Green councillors "are not antisemitic".

Argenzio told local Labour representatives they were being "directed by your national party leader" rather than local concerns.

In a statement on Monday, the council's Labour leader Cllr Fran Belbin said her party would propose on Wednesday that it proceeds as a Labour minority administration.

"We now feel we are at the end of the road with the joint administration," she said.

"Our trust in Sheffield Greens is completely broken," she added, accusing them of a "refusal to stand up for Jewish citizens".

Green Party co-leader Rachel Millward, also the leader of Wealden Council, said: "It is ironic that a Labour prime minister who made a promise to solve problems, not score points, has now shown he is willing to disrupt well-run councils for fear of Green success."

She added: "It is utterly irresponsible to conflate criticism of the actions of the state of Israel with antisemitism. Many Jewish people strongly reject the illegal actions of the current Israeli government."

In Warwick, the local Green party said: "We refuse to condemn a democratically decided policy because of political intimidation."

It urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to "reflect his own words in his actions and allow local Labour groups to decide for themselves".

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Green group leader in Havant Netty Shepherd accused Labour of "performative politics" and said the end of their coalition would be a "complete disaster for residents".

"I am a local government councillor, I worry about people's bins, I worry about generating town centres - foreign policy is nothing to do with my remit," she added.

articles.title: Justin Thomas’ home life in 2026: Inside his $13.5 million Florida waterfront mansion, family routine, personal interests and relaxed lifestyle away from the PGA Tour spotlight
articles.summary: Discover the luxurious lifestyle of golfer Justin Thomas in his $13.5 million Florida waterfront mansion, where family, fashion, and relaxation take center stage away from the PGA Tour.
articles.body: Justin Thomas spends a good part of the year on the road, between tournaments, practice schedules and the routines of an elite golfer. Off the course, however, he lives a much more relaxed lifestyle, where family and the location of his Florida home on the water are priorities.That preference is reflected in the golfer’s reported $13.5 million Jupiter-Tequesta area home. The estate has river frontage, a private dock and is close to South Florida’s golf facilities, allowing for the balance between professional preparation and personal downtime.Inside Justin Thomas’ Florida waterfront mansionThe waterfront estate was reportedly bought by Justin Thomas in 2022 for about $13.5 million, up from his previous Jupiter home, which was valued at around $3.1 million. In the Tequesta-Jupiter area of South Florida, the mansion is more defined by water and privacy than a traditional golf community.The reported 7,600-square-foot property is located on the Loxahatchee River and features approximately 100 feet of riverfront and a private boat dock. These features allow Thomas to enjoy boating and the surrounding waterfront environment when he is not preparing for tournaments.Why does Justin Thomas prefer a waterfront property?Thomas’ selection suits his wish to get away from the pressures of professional golf and be somewhere peaceful. Competing on the PGA Tour for more than 30 weeks a year means a lot of his professional life revolves around golf courses, practice facilities and tournament schedules.At home, the river setting is a different atmosphere. There are chances to spend time on the water instead of golf at the private dock and in the outdoor surroundings.The property also provides easy access to elite golf facilities such as The Bear's Club in Jupiter. This means Thomas can continue his professional training without turning his home life into a sports environment entirely.How Justin Thomas balances golf and family lifeFamily life is an important part of Thomas' routine outside of tournaments. He is married to Jillian Thomas and they have a daughter, Molly Grace. They also have their dog Franklin in their home.Apparently, Thomas prefers a more relaxed routine during his breaks, compared to the tightly managed schedule he follows during tournament weeks. “College football, family time and the simple pleasures of home life are a contrast to the pressure of professional competition.”His life has taken on another dimension with his transition into fatherhood. Family commitments provide him with a chance to take a step back from the constant demands of travel, training and performance expectations.What Justin Thomas enjoys away from golfThomas is a passionate fan of fashion, particularly sneakers and footwear. He reportedly has a collection of popular Jordan releases and designer pieces from Saint Laurent. He’s also mentioned loving the time he spends organizing his closet and putting together casual outfits.The interest gives him a creative outlet away from his day job as a golfer. He has to stick to the sponsorship and tournament rules with his tournament clothing, but in his personal life he has more freedom to express himself.Thomas is a big college football fan as well, especially the Alabama Crimson Tide. Away from the PGA Tour, his ties to the University of Alabama are still a part of his identity.His houses also reportedly had entertainment areas with multiple televisions and Alabama-themed pool tables. These features are a testament to his love of watching sports and kicking back with friends and family.Thomas' lifestyle also reflects the casual waterfront culture in and around Jupiter. His tastes at the table have been tied to local spots such as Square Grouper Tiki Bar and U-Tiki Beach.They have a relaxed feel that is a nice contrast to the programmed schedules and hospitality packages that accompany major golf tournaments.Fundamentally, Thomas’ Florida home is more than just a luxury property. The waterfront setting, family atmosphere and entertainment facilities provide a personal escape from the professional game of golf. The PGA Tour necessitates consistency, prep, and endless travel, but his non-competitive life offers him family, fashion, football, and the South Florida lifestyle.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Curry explodes after halftime to lead Warriors to 5th straight win
articles.summary: Curry took over when the Dubs needed it most.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The Warriors didn't have Steph Curry or Draymond Green when they visited the Suns on the second half of a back-to-back last weekend.

Hosting the Suns, again coming off a game the previous night, Golden State set things up to make sure its two veteran stars would be available for the rematch.

The training staff's best efforts ended up for naught.

After sitting out Sunday's win over the Clippers, Green spent most of the second half Monday night in the locker room. Green was ejected two minutes into the second half.

And that was precisely when the game turned for the Warriors, who pulled out a 116-113 win after falling behind by as many as 17 points and not holding a lead until the fourth quarter.

The Warriors have won five straight since their 131-122 loss in Phoenix last Saturday.

When Green was tossed from the game, Golden State trailed 68-57. Immediately after play resumed, the Warriors' energy changed and they went on a 16-5 run to tie the score at 73.

Curry didn't exactly seem freshly rested as he struggled for nine points in the first half. But he exploded for 25 after halftime to lead the Warriors, finishing with 34.

After going off for 37 points without Curry the previous night and leading the Warriors with 26 the last time they faced Phoenix, Yaxel Lendeborg was contained to 16 on 3-of-10 shooting.

But the Warriors didn't shy away from running their offense from the rookie with Curry off the floor, and his eight second-half free throws on nine attempts kept the Suns at bay.

With 44 and 31 his past two games, Curry notched the 25th streak of his career of three straight games with 30 or more in the scoring column. In six games this season, Curry has scored at least 20 in all of them, averaging 30.0, trailing only Anthony Edwards and Luka Doncic.

With Devin Booker pouring in 26 to lead the Suns and Mikal Bridges adding 21, Curry couldn't do it by himself. He got an unlikely assist in the form of center Charles Bassey, who picked up many of Green's second-half minutes to finish with a career-best 19 on 7-of-10 shooting.

Brandin Podziemski also contributed 20 points, including 14 after halftime. He tied the game at 93 on the Warriors' final possession of the third quarter on a kickout from Lendeborg.

A cutting Bassey converted one of Curry's team-high seven assists on the Warriors' first possession of the fourth quarter that gave them their first lead of the game, 95-93, and the margin never got wider than seven in either direction the rest of the way.

The Warriors followed in Curry's footsteps in the first half, knocking down just two of their first 17 attempts from 3. But the ball started falling for Curry and his teammates after halftime.

Golden State drained 11 of its final 25 attempts from 3, including five from Curry.

articles.title: Warriors on a roll, get fifth straight win behind Steph Curry's 34-point night
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors win their fifth-consecutive contest, defeating Suns, 116-113 on Monday, Nov. 2 at Chase Center.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO ― The Golden State Warriors have rattled off five consecutive wins following their hard-fought 116-113 win against the Phoenix Suns on Monday, Nov. 2 at Chase Center.

Warriors guard Stephen Curry led the way with 34 points and seven assists, while backcourt running mate Brandin Podziemski dropped 20 points on 50% shooting in the game.

There was no love lost between these two teams, which saw each other on Oct. 24 when the Suns got the upper hand. In the rematch, it was the Warriors who came with energy and fight.

Warriors forward Draymond Green was ejected for the first time this season following a foul against Suns center Khaman Maluach when afterward Green committed a takedown on Maluach. Suns guard Dillon Brooks confronted Green about the push and the two began a shoving match before receiving double technical fouls.

Golden State trailed by 11 points at the time of the technical foul and proceeded to go on a run to fight back into the game before taking over, putting up 42 points in the third period to tie the game 93-93.

The Warriors received a major boost from Charles Bassey, who was effective off the bench scoring 17 points and pulling down 8 rebounds in 23 minutes. Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 16 points on 3-of-10 shooting, grabbing five rebounds and five assists.

"Bass was great. What a big night for him," Kerr said after the game. "The rebounding, the scoring. You know he and Yaxel have a really good connection. The pick-and-roll game. He gives him a lot of threat. Yaxel sees the floor so well and he's so big that he finds him when he's behind the defense."

Golden State will host the Miami Heat on Thursday, Nov. 5 , beginning at 7 p.m. PT (10 p.m. ET).

articles.title: Jon Rahm: "No me gustaba hacia donde iba el LIV Golf 2.0"
articles.standfirst: El de Barrika explica su renuncia a seguir en la liga alternativa, aunque valora como "muy positiva" sus tres años. Aún no sabe dónde jugará en 2027, pero lo dibuja cercano al DP World Tour
articles.summary: El de Barrika explica su renuncia a seguir en la liga alternativa, aunque valora como "muy positiva" sus tres años. Aún no sabe dónde jugará en 2027, pero lo dibuja cercano al DP World Tour
articles.body: Jon Rahm llegó a Yas Links en Abu Dhabi con el jet lag a cuestas, una hija más, sin apenas un swing en casi dos meses y con más preguntas que certezas sobre su calendario de 2027. En su primera rueda de prensa tras desvincularse de LIV Golf, el de Barrika no esquivó ningún tema: explicó por qué rechazó las condiciones de la nueva etapa de la liga saudí, admitió cierta frustración económica y abrió la puerta a pasar un año completo en el DP World Tour. Rahm calificó sus tres años en LIV como “una experiencia maravillosa” y destacó los buenos resultados, tanto individuales como por equipos. Pero el nuevo formato no le convenció. “Por muy a gusto que estuviera con el proyecto en LIV 1.0, no me hacía ilusión los cambios de la 2.0 y no estaba dispuesto a seguir ese camino”, explicó. Al ser interpelado por los motivos concretos, señaló la incertidumbre: “Había demasiadas incógnitas entonces y todavía hay unas cuantas”. Además, percibió un alejamiento del golf por equipos y de los rasgos distintivos de la liga: “Se convertía más en un circuito normal”. Cuando se le preguntó si sintió frustración por no recibir lo que se acordó inicialmente hace tres años, y si otros jugadores dejaron dinero sobre la mesa al marcharse, la respuesta fue lacónica: un “no”. Sobre si la marcha de tantos jugadores indica que LIV no puede sobrevivir en su forma actual, evitó pronunciarse. Cree que habrá quien quiera continuar y nuevos jugadores con oportunidades, pero reconoció que hace tiempo que no participa en reuniones sobre los detalles de la 2.0. Rahm admitió también el desgaste mental de todo el proceso: “Lo quieras admitir o no, es ruido en tu cabeza. Ha quitado atención y esfuerzo de lo que quiero hacer, y en ese sentido ha sido una distracción, sin duda”. El español llega como el hombre del corte, en el puesto 51 de la clasificación, cuando solo pasan los 50 mejores a la semana siguiente en la final de Dubai del DP World Tour. Admitió que es una situación inédita: “No sé si alguna vez ha pasado”. Aun así, quitó dramatismo. Todos los participantes suman puntos esta semana y, a su juicio, no necesita una actuación estelar. “Si juego sólido, sé cómo puedo jugar al golf, debería jugar la semana que viene”, aseguró, apuntando además que varios jugadores han decidido no disputar estas dos citas, lo que mejora las probabilidades. El futuro en Estados Unidos sigue en el aire. Rahm todavía no ha hablado con el PGA Tour para saber si existe un camino de vuelta. “A día de hoy no sé cómo será 2027”, reconoció. Su plan, hasta tener claridad, es jugar el año en el DP World Tour y ya estudia el calendario para diseñar “un año un poco distinto a los anteriores”. Mencionó el caso de Brooks Koepka, que pudo regresar “bajo ciertas circunstancias”, aunque duda de que se le ofrezca lo mismo. Con todo, si tuviera que cumplir una suspensión de un año, lo ve con optimismo: “Es una buena posición que el peor escenario sea jugar un año entero en un gran circuito”. Preguntado si aceptaría las mismas condiciones que Koepka, respondió: “Seguramente sí. ¿Por qué no?”, aunque insistió en que duda mucho de que le ofrezcan el mismo trato. En cualquier caso, promete apoyar al DP World Tour: aunque regrese al PGA Tour, seguirá jugando eventos europeos, “como he hecho en el pasado y quizá algunos más”. Sobre la gira por Oriente Medio, no descarta jugar Dubái, Bahréin y Qatar, aunque dice que no encadenaría cuatro torneos seguidos tras la Team Cup. Rahm reveló que en Wentworth, su última aparición, tenía la cabeza en otro lado de ahí su nefasto resultado. Había preocupación por un posible adelanto del parto y no quería perderse lo que probablemente sea el último nacimiento de la familia. “Había tenido la suerte de estar en casa en los tres partos anteriores”. Con el cuarto hijo, por primera vez pudo estar la primera semana en casa: “En los tres anteriores, cuando llegamos del hospital, cogí mi bolsa y me fui”. Ayudó con los otros tres hijos, los llevó al colegio y vivió “lo que hace cualquier otro padre”. El coste deportivo es evidente: “Después de un vuelo largo, decir que estoy ‘oxidado’ es quedarse corto. Además, dedicó un reconocimiento especial a su mujer, Kelley: “Hay que tener una pareja fuerte para asumir tanto. He tenido mucha suerte”.

articles.title: Jon Rahm uncertain about PGA Tour future after LIV Golf exit but would accept deal similar to Brooks Koepka to return
articles.summary: Jon Rahm says his route back to the PGA Tour is uncertain and he has not yet had clarity on what that looks like; he declined the Returning Member Program, which Brooks Koepka chose to take in January; watch the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Rahm quit LIV Golf after deeming the terms offered for the proposed relaunch of the breakaway series "unacceptable" .

This occurred when LIV Golf was going through Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the US after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support at the end of the season, having invested $5bn (£3.7bn) over four years.

Having now left LIV, Rahm is set to return to play on the DP World Tour in 2027, but expressed some uncertainty over his future, admitting he has not yet spoken to the PGA Tour about what a return could look like.

At the beginning of 2026, Rahm declined the PGA Tour's offer of reinstatement through a specially created Returning Member Program, which was made available to him, Bryson DeChambeau, Cameron Smith and Brooks Koepka.

Koepka was the only player to sign up to the Returning Member Program.

"As of right now, I really don't know what 2027 is going to look like for me," Rahm said, speaking ahead of the DP World Tour's Abu Dhabi Championship, live on Sky Sports from Thursday.

"I have yet to have a discussion with the PGA Tour to see if there's any path back for next year, so I don't know.

"Until I get clarity on that, my plan would be to spend a year on the DP World Tour. I'm looking forward to it.

"Obviously, Brooks [Koepka] was able to go back through certain circumstances.

"I don't know if the possibility of that would be open for me or not."

As part of the Returning Member Program, Koepka returned to the PGA Tour under certain conditions , with the American instructed to make a $5m (£3.7m) charitable donation and was excluded from earning equity on the PGA Tour for the next five years.

At present, Rahm will face a one-year suspension from the PGA Tour before he is eligible to win back his card.

"If I have to fulfil a one-year suspension, it's a pretty good position to be in. Worst-case scenario, I get to play in a wonderful tour [the DP World Tour] for a whole year," Rahm added.

"I seriously doubt I will get offered the same deals that Brooks did. But if I got offered exactly the same penalties as him, I probably would do it, yes."

Rahm, who tees up at this week's Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, reflected on his time with LIV Golf positively, but he admitted he did not like the direction the new iteration of the league was heading in, and in the end, it was not much of a "consideration" on whether to stay.

For Rahm, a move away from the team golf element was a big factor.

"Well, I would say I can only reflect on those three years as a positive. It was a wonderful experience; I played a lot of good golf, obviously, individually and as a team. We did great," he added.

"Why did I reject the terms? As much as I liked the project and the idea on, let's say, LIV 1.0, I wasn't thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0, and I just wasn't willing to follow that path.

"It wasn't anything special, anything that stood out. I didn't like what they were going with 2.0.

"There were too many unknowns at the time, and there's still quite a few.

"It seemed like it was going a bit away from team golf and some of the things that made LIV. It just became more of a regular tour.

"It wasn't really ever much of a consideration, to be honest."

"I don't know what is in store for us," he continued. "We know what they did with Brooks. This is different circumstances. I don't know what things are going to look like. Koepka was permitted to return to the PGA Tour in January under a new Returning Member Program, which Schlabach said "allowed LIV golfers who have been away from the tour for at least two years -- and who won the Players Championship or one of the four majors (the Masters, PGA Championship, U.S. Open and Open Championship) since 2022 -- to return under certain conditions and with severe financial penalties." articles.title: Ryder Cup: Lee Westwood has 'no regrets' about turning down chance to captain Team Europe to play on LIV Golf
articles.summary: Lee Westwood was one of the candidates to captain Team Europe at the 2023 Ryder Cup before he joined LIV Golf; Westwood is yet to sign with LIV 2.0 and says the breakaway league are yet to present him with "anything agreeable"
articles.body:
During a wide-ranging interview on The Chipping Forecast podcast , the 53-year-old said he was currently "unemployed" and added LIV 2.0 had not presented him with "anything agreeable" for the league's proposed relaunch in 2027.

Westwood has represented Team Europe at the Ryder Cup on 11 occasions, having tied Sir Nick Faldo for the most appearances at the biennial tournament during his last outing at Whistling Straits in 2021.

Having worked as a vice-captain under Thomas Bjørn at the 2018 Ryder Cup in France, the Englishman was one of the DP World Tour's leading candidates to be appointed captain for the tournament in Rome in 2023.

"Whistling Straights had happened and then quite shortly after that I had a conversation with [DP World Tour chief executive] Guy Kinnings, where he talked about the Ryder Cup captaincy and the captain in Italy," Westwood, who joined LIV Golf in 2022, said.

"It was put to me whether I'd like to be Ryder Cup captain, and I had started discussions with LIV. I think I asked: 'If I did go to LIV, could I still be Ryder Cup captain?'

"They didn't say no, but it was made clear that there would be very little chance of it, and I made the decision to go to LIV.

"You make calls in life, don't you?" Westwood added. "You make a choice, and I have no regrets over the choice I made."

The DP World Tour dictates a player cannot be a European Ryder Cup captain or vice-captain if they decline membership to the tour or fail to fulfil their minimum event obligations.

Henrik Stenson was later named captain for 2023 before he also joined LIV Golf, with the baton ultimately being handed to Luke Donald.

Westwood, who jointly holds the record for the most appearances for Europe at a Ryder Cup, was asked whether he would consider being captain in the future.

"I don't know, I get asked that question a lot," Westwood said. "I've always just wanted to play, I love playing golf.

"When I was vice captain, everybody has a little say in the team room, and I said to the guys: 'You better enjoy it as much as you can because when it's gone, you really miss it, and I'll tell you one thing worse than playing practice rounds in a Ryder Cup is watching other people playing practice rounds in a Ryder Cup.'

"I loved being a Ryder Cup player and getting in that environment. I don't know whether I'd have been a good Ryder Cup captain, because of what I said in France. I don't know whether I would have liked watching."

Delving further, Westwood said: "I'm not good at really pushing control.

"That's one of the reasons I started playing golf, I played a lot of football and rugby and cricket before taking up golf. The reason I enjoy playing golf is because the buck stops with me.

"I didn't want to have to rely on other people and that probably goes back to a little bit of the reason why the Ryder Cup captaincy wasn't really that higher priority.

"When push came to shove, it wasn't the be-all and end-all for me. I'm not sure I wanted it enough."

LIV Golfers have a deadline of November 16 to reapply for their DP World Tour memberships, and Westwood says he is deliberating whether to do so.

Should he reapply, he would face a 10-tournament suspension for his decision to resign his DP World Tour membership.

"I haven't signed up to anything anywhere, I haven't made a decision on anything yet," Westwood said.

"I am yet to have everything put in front of me and I have not really had any dialogue with the DP World Tour.

"I know if I sign up, I've then got to serve a 10-tournament suspension. I've looked at the schedule, and I feel like the first event I could play in on the DP World Tour will be the Turkish Airlines Open, which is the first week in May, so I haven't looked any further.

"There's nothing that's been presented to me that was agreeable for LIV 2.0. There are still a lot of things that would need fine-tuning; deadlines have come and gone, and I've heard nothing on whether I have to sign or not.

"I haven't signed [for] 2.0. So, I literally am unemployed."

articles.title: It’s Just One Game, BUT……
articles.summary: Let’s overreact to the first game of a new Marquette men’s basketball season, shall we?
articles.body:
And now, with the first Marquette men's basketball game of the season in the books, let's overreact to what we saw in the 40 minutes of action at Fiserv Forum against Mercyhurst.

Something has to be done about the three-point shooting.

I don't have the patience to go back through chart every single long range attempt that Marquette fired off on Monday night to tell you whether or not MU shot nothing but open catch-and-shoot jumpers and we all just have to live with the results. What I can tell you is that 4-for-21 from behind the three-point line is 19.0% and that is not going to cut it against a team that looks like they can tie their own shoes on the first try.

Now, sure, some caveats. Odds are we're going to see Marquette's starting five play a lot more minutes on a nightly basis. Sananda Fru led the crew here with just 23 minutes, and Damarius Owens didn't even clear 17. Those five — four, really, because Fru didn't attempt a triple — shot 3-for-10 behind the arc. If we shuttle some of the 1-for-11 shooting from everyone else over to Nigel James, Adrien Stevens, and Royce Parham, odds are it won't be 1-for-11 much longer. Yes, Stevens missed all three of his attempts. He'll be fine eventually.

Who might not be fine is Michael Phillips, who went 1-for-5 and HOO BOY, some of his misses were UGLY. Alex Egbuonu went 0-for-3 after looking pretty solid on his stroke against Michigan State. That's 1-for-8 just on those two guys, so that's seven of MU's 17 misses right there. This will all likely balance out…. but this 19% stuff can't happen again.

I've been sitting back here watching Clark against Green Bay and Michigan State insisting that the best we can do is mark him as totally acceptable to give Sananda Fru a breather. He's been looking fine, there's no reason to heap expectation on him when as recently as March he was unable to play in consecutive games much less do anything productive in them.

I might have to abandon my hold call on Josh Clark's expectations.

TO BE CLEAR ABOUT THIS: Mercyhurst rosters one guy taller than 6'8" and that one guy 1) is 6'9" and thus four inches shorter than Clark and 2) played a total of 10 minutes on Monday night. Please take that into account when I say the following:

Josh Clark played 16 minutes off the bench and tallied up a TEAM HIGH 18 points on 8-for-9 shooting, grabbed seven rebounds, dished an assist, and swatted three shots, including an incredibly dominant, waited til the shot was out of the guy's hand, leapt, and pitched that thing into the third row block in the second half. He never played 16 minutes in a game last year, coming closest with 14 in an 89-49 win over Little Rock. He never touched double digits in scoring, getting to six twice, once versus Little Rock and once in 13 minutes against UConn on the road.

It's just one game, but his rebounding rates for this one game are really not that far off what he was doing in limited minutes last season.

Sananda Fru can do more as a basketball player than Clark can at this point, and at the end of the day, I think that head coach Shaka Smart is going to lean in that direction. And maybe this is more Mercyhurst has a roster of guys giving up 5 inches to Clark than anything else.

But if this is remotely close to real…. watch out.

23 minutes, 12 points on 4-for-6 shooting, team high 12 rebounds, including seven on the offensive end, one assist, tied with Clark for team high in blocks with three, one steal. If Shaka Smart had let him run wild for a playing time closer to 30 minutes like we can probably expect to see from Fru more often than not, that's a 25% bump to his PT and thus his stats. 15 & 15, maybe another assist and a steal, another block? Again, as I mentioned with Clark's unreal night, maybe this is all just a by-product of Mercyhurst not having guys who can literally measure up next to Fru in height.

But this Sananda Fru looked better than what his stats at Louisville indicated. Clearly there was some kind of disconnect between what's best for Fru as a player and what UL head coach Pat Kelsey wants his big man to do, and that's why Fru isn't a Cardinal any more. I'm willing to believe he can do more and be more than his 2025-26 stat profile says he can be…. so where exactly is the limit on that?

The possessions where Marquette gets stuck in neutral on offense have to stop.

I can only remember one on Monday night. All of a sudden, the shot clock drifts under 10, and MU was nowhere close to finding a useful shot. Clock continues to wind, Nigel James gets it late in the clock, and has to half-ass force something together to get a shot off in time.

I only remember the one, which, y'know, sometimes when you're up big — the one I remember was in the second half in front of MU's bench — you get a little too patient, a little too lax, not quite as quick and decisive as you need to be, and now there's six seconds left on the shot clock and you pitch it to the preseason all-Big East First Teamer to make something happen. Okay. It happens. I'm willing to say ah, well, 64 possessions, one wasn't fun.

But I saw a lot of those "uh, now what?" type of possessions against Green Bay and Michigan State. Those types of possessions were part of the reason why MU was only up five at the half on the Phoenix and part of the reason why Michigan State sliced a double digit margin down to just five points in the exhibition games. Marquette is supposed to beat Green Bay, and Marquette should beat teams that play as poorly as Michigan State played, even if both games were exhibitions. Mission accomplished, even with the problems that developed again and again.

Eventually this season, Marquette is going to face a good team throwing their A game at the Golden Eagles. That might be coming up next Wednesday in Ann Arbor against Michigan. If we get too many of those stuck in neutral possessions, things can turn against Marquette in a hurry. As a team that has a Lost In The Fight mantra and a Play With Violence mantra, even one of these types of offensive possessions feels like too many in one game.

The writing is on the wall for Ian Miletic, and probably for Nash Walker.

Freshman Ethan Johnston subbed into the game at the 9:17 mark of the first half with Marquette up 20-8. He was the last sub into the game that I was completely expecting to see in the opener. MU was up 20 for the first time with 3:37 left before the break, they were up 22 at intermission, they were up 30 with 16:49 left in the second half, and they were up 40 for the first time with 8:04 left to go.

Ian Miletic checked in at the 4:28 mark of the second half with the score sitting at 71-29, Marquette by 42. Nash Walker came in at the under-4 media timeout, 3:51 to go, same score as when Miletic checked in 40-ish seconds earlier.

Marquette lost the time that those two played by a score of 14-7. 10-6 before Braeden Brenn and Colton Crowdis checked in for the Human Victory Cigar Formation with 49 seconds left.

If there was an inkling of an idea inside Shaka Smart's head that he was curious to find out if he could get anything at all out of Miletic or Walker this season, they would have played at nearly literally any other point in the game. For sure after Johnston checked in. Definitely in the second half long before there was just four minutes remaining. "Hey, we're up 30, who cares, let's give Ian five minutes here."

Marquette had their worst stretch of the game with them on the floor against an opponent that was wildly in over their head from Minute #1.

What's the over/under on Marquette home games with Milwaukee Brewers in attendance for the rest of the season?

In case you missed it, left fielder Jackson Chourio, second baseman (and now National League MVP finalist!) Brice Turang, and bullpen catcher Christian Correa from YOUR 2026 World Series Champion Milwaukee Brewers pulled up on Monday night. They got to sit courtside near the MU bench in the seats where you can commonly find Marquette President Kimo Ah Yun and assorted special guests.

As the Scrambled Eggs podcast noted in their season preview episode that published on Monday morning, it would be neat to see the champs stop in for a vist at some point this season. And so, we checked that box off in Game #1.

That's just two of the players on the active roster, though. There's still another 17 home games to go, although the last three are after spring training starts. Figure it's likely that Marquette won't bring anyone to the McGuire Center on Friday, and none of the Brewers will make it to any of the home games in the second half of February.

That's 13 other home games. Calculate in the fact that these guys have winter training situations and Christmas and so on, let's set it at +/- 4.5 games with at least one Brewers player or manager Pat Murphy in attendance. Which side of that do you want to take?

That's my overreactions for Game #1 of the 2026-27 Marquette men's basketball season. What are yours? Fire away in the comments, let's see whatcha got.

articles.summary: Former world number one Lee Westwood says he has not signed for LIV 2.0, while two-time major champion Jon Rahm did not want to "follow the path" of the proposed version.
articles.body:
Lee Westwood says he has not signed for LIV 2.0 or held talks with the DP World Tour about a return, leaving the European Ryder Cup legend "unemployed" as he considers his future.

The 53-year-old Englishman was among the high-profile players lured to LIV Golf when the controversial Saudi-backed breakaway tour began in 2022.

LIV's future remains unclear after Saudi's Public Investment Fund (PIF) withdrew its backing - having pumped in more than $5bn (£3.8bn) - and led to the league filing for bankruptcy protection last month.

In an interview with The Chipping Forecast podcast, , external Westwood said: "I'm currently unemployed.

"There hasn't been anything presented to me that is agreeable for LIV 2.0, there are still a lot of things on that which need fine-tuning. I haven't signed for 2.0. I haven't signed anything."

Westwood has been criticised for pursuing the vast sums of money offered by LIV, while further antagonising some people with his staunch defence of the league during exchanges on social media.

The move cost him the chance to captain the European Ryder Cup team in 2023, but he says he would have "been stupid" not to set himself up financially for life.

"I've made a fortune over the last four and a half years," added Westwood, who is reported to have won £16m in prize money on the LIV tour.

"I don't really have to play golf again, but I still love playing golf so it's given [me] the option what to do over the next few years."

Rahm unwilling to 'follow path' of LIV 2.0

Fellow European Ryder Cup player Jon Rahm says he decided to leave LIV because he "wasn't willing to follow the path" taken by the league as it fights for survival.

It was the first time the 31-year-old Spaniard has spoken publicly since securing his exit from the series in October by reaching a separation agreement.

Rahm was the reigning Masters champion when he was convinced to join LIV - a seismic move which underlined the scale of the league's ambition.

"As much as I liked the project and the idea on, let's say, LIV 1.0, I wasn't thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0," Rahm said at the Abu Dhabi Championship, his first event since leaving LIV.

"It wasn't anything special, anything that stood out. I just didn't like where they were going with 2.0."

Rahm joined LIV in a deal worth a reported $300m (£222m), only to leave last month with $100m (£75m) - according to ESPN - owed on the remainder of the contract.

"There were too many unknowns," added the two-time major winner. "It seemed like it was going a bit away from team golf.

"It became more of a regular tournament. It wasn't really ever much of a consideration."

Rahm is among several big-name players to leave LIV in recent weeks, along with Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton and Graeme McDowell.

Westwood remains unsure what he will do next, but he does believe the proposed LIV 2.0 still has the potential to thrive.

"With the way the business was structured, there was too much waste really," he said.

"I think there is a business there - if LIV 2.0 gets off the ground it will be a successful business. Can they get the players? Time will tell."

What Westwood must do to rejoin DP World Tour

If Westwood does not rejoin LIV, the former world number one could look for a way back to the DP World Tour.
