articles.standfirst: Una tormenta eléctrica sorprendió a la joven mientras competía en un torneo
articles.summary: Una tormenta eléctrica sorprendió a la joven mientras competía en un torneo
articles.body: Aeyavarin 'Aeya' Pradubyart, golfista tailandesa de 15 años, falleció el lunes a consecuencia de haber sido alcanzada por un rayo el domingo mientras disputaba un torneo juvenil en la provincia de Chachoengsao, al sureste de Bangkok, según informó el periódico local Nation. El incidente ocurrió alrededor de las 4 de la tarde, mientras Aeyavarin jugaba el hoyo 11 en un campo de golf del condado de Bang Nam Priao. Aeyavarin y su caddie, Saithan, de 31 años, fueron alcanzados por un rayo durante una tormenta eléctrica La golfista fue reanimada en un primer momento, pero su estado empeoró durante la noche. La madre de la golfista, que se encontraba en el club, explicó que una hora antes ya se escucharon los primeros truenos, pero los organizadores no quisieron suspender el juego. El padre, trabajado en Myanmar, llegó justo a tiempo para darle el último adiós. La abuela materna de la joven, Aphorn, incidió en que los organizadores permitieron que los golfistas continuaran jugando, a pesar de dos rayos previos, como si quisiesen acabar la competición a toda costa. Según el familiar, la joven sufrió quemaduras en el lado derecho de la cabeza, el cuerpo, los brazos y las piernas. Su sombrero también quedó devastado Asimismo, recalcó que el traslado al hospital se retrasó considerablemente porque el campo de golf no disponía de ambulancia. Aeyavarin era una golfista de nivel provincial que había ganado torneos locales. Sus actuaciones le habían valido la selección como reserva del equipo provincial de golf de Chon Buri. Entre los golfistas profesionales los dos episodios más conocidos sucedieron en 1975, cuando Lee Trevino, Jerry Heard, Tony Jacklin y Bobby Nichols fueron alcanzados en el mismo torneo, el Western Open, cuando un rayo cayó en un lago y se propagó hacia donde estaban ellos, y Retief Goosen, que en 1984, sufrió la descarga de un rayo cuando jugaba un torneo juvenil. Le desintegró toda la ropa y quedó tocado de un oído para siempre.

articles.title: Jon Rahm doesn't know if he has 'path back' to PGA Tour from LIV in 2027, is willing to accept same penalties as Brooks Koepka
articles.summary: Rahm has officially cut ties with LIV Golf, but hasn't spoken with the PGA Tour about a return next season.
articles.body:
Jon Rahm announced on Oct. 7 that he was leaving LIV Golf amid the golf league's bankruptcy hearings and financial uncertainty as it transitions to LIV Golf 2.0.

Rahm spoke with media on Tuesday for the first time since his decision to leave LIV Golf. He'd like to play on the PGA Tour in 2027, but he's not sure if he has a "path back."

If he doesn't, Rahm says that he'll play next year on the DP World Tour, Europe's top men's professional golf league. The top 10 players at the end of a DP World Tour season earn a PGA Tour card .

Rahm unclear on his 'path back' to PGA Tour

Rahm made his comments from Yas Links in Abu Dhabi for a stop on the DP World Tour Playoffs.

"I have yet to have a discussion with the PGA Tour to see if there's any path back for next year," Rahm said, per Golf Week . "So I don't know, as of right now. Until I get clarity on that, yeah, my plan would be to spend the year on the DP World Tour, and I'm looking forward to it."

What a path back to the PGA Tour absent earning his way on the DP World Tour would look like is unclear. When asked, Rahm said that he'd likely be willing to accept the same penalties that Brooks Koepka did upon his return to the tour from LIV Golf. But he doesn't expect to receive that offer.

"Most likely, yeah. Why not?" Rahm said of returning under the same terms as Koepka. "Yeah, but it's a big if. "I seriously doubt I get offered the same deal that Brooks did. But yeah, if I got offered exactly the same penalties as him, I probably would do it, yes."

"Most likely, yeah. Why not?" Rahm said of returning under the same terms as Koepka. "Yeah, but it's a big if.

"I seriously doubt I get offered the same deal that Brooks did. But yeah, if I got offered exactly the same penalties as him, I probably would do it, yes."

Koepka's return came at a cost of up to $85 million in earnings

Koepka announced his return to the PGA Tour from LIV Golf in January via the Tour's "Returning Members Program." At the time, the PGA Tour offered immediate reinstatement to a select group of players who had won either The Players Championship, Masters, PGA Championship, U.S. Open or British Open Championship between 2022 and 2025.

The reinstatement offer came with substantial penalties including a five-year forfeiture of participation in the player equity program, worth up to an estimated $85 million in earnings for a player of Koepka's caliber. The PGA Tour outlined those penalties upon Koepka's return.

"Its strict limitations, which Brooks has agreed to, include a five-year forfeiture of potential equity in the PGA Tour's player equity program, representing one of the largest financial repercussions in professional sports history, with estimations that he could miss out on approximately $50-85 million in potential earnings, depending on his competitive performance and the growth of the Tour. "At the request of the PGA Tour, Brooks has also agreed to make a $5 million charitable contribution, the recipient(s) of which will be determined jointly."

"Its strict limitations, which Brooks has agreed to, include a five-year forfeiture of potential equity in the PGA Tour's player equity program, representing one of the largest financial repercussions in professional sports history, with estimations that he could miss out on approximately $50-85 million in potential earnings, depending on his competitive performance and the growth of the Tour.

"At the request of the PGA Tour, Brooks has also agreed to make a $5 million charitable contribution, the recipient(s) of which will be determined jointly."

Patrick Reed's path includes DP World Tour and equity penalty

Koepka was the only player to return from LIV Golf under those terms before the Feb. 2 expiration date the PGA Tour set on its "Returning Members Program." Rahm would have qualified for the program's terms due to his 2023 Masters win had he chosen to accept them when they were offered.

Patrick Reed was not eligible for the "Returning Member's Program." Instead, he left the LIV tour in Aug. 2025, and has since been playing the DP World Tour as he served what was essentially a one-year suspension, which ended on Aug. 25. He's ranked No. 2 as of Tuesday and has officially earned his PGA Tour card. When he returns to the PGA Tour, he'll be subject to the same forfeiture of the player equity program as Koepka.

Rahm on Tuesday floated skipping the DP Tour World Tour path that Reed is taking, but is understandably skeptical in the PGA Tour's interest in such a proposal.

Bryson DeChambeau, meanwhile, has indicated that he plans to take part in LIV Golf 2.0. DeChambeau has arguably been the league's most prominent player and was also eligible for the PGA Tour's "Returning Members Program."

The penalties for returning LIV golfers are in place due to the significant rift caused by players defecting from the PGA Tour to LIV Golf starting in 2022. LIV was an upstart golf league offering lucrative pay packages to siphon players off the PGA Tour in a threat to the U.S. tour's health and bottom line.

The initial iteration of LIV Golf was funded by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, bringing with it concerns of sportswashing the nation's human rights violations . The fund has since withdrawn its financial support, putting LIV Golf's future in peril.

articles.title: Warriors Proposed To Trade Kristaps Porzingis For NBA’s Best Rebounder
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors trade for Domantas Sabonis, the NBA's top rebounder, as a Kristaps Porzingis replacement in a new proposed idea. The post Warriors...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors lack frontcourt depth, and the absence of Kristaps Porzingis to begin the year has been a big hit for the team hoping to stay competitive in the final seasons left in the Stephen Curry era.

The Warriors are reportedly exploring a Porzingis trade, and with that, a few replacement options have emerged as names the team could go after to capitalize on the time left they have with Curry.

With that, one big man in particular who remains a top Warriors trade target is Domantas Sabonis of the Sacramento Kings, and in a new proposal, Golden State takes a big risk to add the center, who is not happy playing for his current team, to land a solid Porzingis replacement.

Writing for Bleacher Report amid Golden State's need to upgrade the frontcourt and add a Porzingis replacement, Andy Bailey offered up a Warriors trade proposal that sees the team add Sabonis from the Kings.

Golden State Warriors Receive: Domantas Sabonis

Sacramento Kings Receive: Draymond Green (trade-eligible on December 15), Kristaps Porziņģis, Will Richard and a top-four protected 2032 first-round pick

"The Golden State Warriors' better-than-expected start makes a Draymond Green trade harder to imagine, but they look like a near-ideal landing spot for Sabonis, and they simply can't get him without including Green or Jimmy Butler," he wrote. "The more logical approach, assuming the Warriors really want to chase one more title with Stephen Curry, is to pair Green's salary with the Kristaps Porziņģis contract, which was essentially designed to be a human trade exception."

Moving Green might be difficult for the Warriors, but as seen with his recent ejection , there's clearly still some major holes in his game, as he isn't the same type of player he was during the team's dynasty run a decade ago.

Sabonis is also reportedly frustrated in Sacramento right now, and if he is available in a trade for a team like Golden State, he could be a huge upgrade, especially with Porzingis still out.

"Sabonis would be a dramatic upgrade over Green in scoring and rebounding. He's at least as good a passer (though maybe not quite as good a creator). And it's easy to imagine the fit between him and Yaxel Lendeborg. Curry's off-ball movement around either (or both) of those interior hubs would be nearly impossible to stop," Bailey added.

"It's maybe a harder sell on the other side of the deal. Neither vet seems like a longterm option for Sacramento, but Green's deal is expiring and Porziņģis' is only guaranteed for $3 million. They represent an opportunity for flexibility, while Sabonis' deal is guaranteed for $48.6 million next season."

A Warriors trade proposal like this one, though risky, could be the franchise's best option to move on from Porzingis while staying competitive after going on a hot streak to begin the 2026-27 season.

Why Golden State Lands A Kristaps Porzingis Replacement

As mentioned, the Warriors are reportedly exploring the possibility of trading Porzingis, as he remains out indefinitely with the POTS illness he picked up a few years ago, and has yet to spend pretty much any time with the team.

"Golden State has started exploring trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis, who is now seriously contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autoimmune condition termed as POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome), sources tell ESPN," Shams Charania wrote in a post on X.

"Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million extension with the team in June, but only $3 million of the $20 million in the second season is guaranteed, essentially making it an expiring contract. The front office strategically designed the extension without a raise between the two seasons, keeping him immediately trade-eligible instead of needing to wait until mid-December," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote in subsequent reporting.

With that, Sabonis becomes a very realistic replacement option. He isn't the same caliber player he was a few seasons ago, but remains an offensive hub who could help the Warriors stay competitive over the next few seasons. The center's scoring numbers are down, but he is averaging a league-leading 14.6 rebounds , along with 6.9 assists, while shooting 71.2% so far this year.

His trade value might be low right now, and though the Warriors would have to give up Green in a trade to match salaries, this could be the one final risk Golden State takes to give Curry another shot at leading the team to a fifth title.

Just a trade idea, but perhaps one the Warriors should entertain, as Porzingis remains out, and there's no timeline for when or if he'll ever play in the Bay Area again.

articles.title: Roberson, Nelson lead No. 4 Duke past Green Bay 76-60 to open season
articles.summary: No. 4 Duke's Arianna Roberson led the way for the Blue Devils in their season opener win over Green Bay on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Arianna Roberson had 15 points and four blocked shots while No. 4 Duke took control after halftime to beat Green Bay 76-60 in Tuesday night's opener for both teams.

Riley Nelson also scored 15 for the Blue Devils, the preseason favorite to win a third straight Atlantic Coast Conference title. Duke played without preseason all-ACC pick Toby Fournier, with coach Kara Lawson saying afterward that the 6-foot-2 forward who was last year's leading scorer (17.3) and rebounder (7.9) is dealing with a lower-leg injury. Lawson said she hopes Fournier is back soon but said there is no specific timetable yet.

Duke had a tussle on its hands in the first half, leading just 33-31 at halftime against the preseason pick to win the Horizon League title for a fourth straight year.

But the Blue Devils did a better job asserting themselves inside after halftime, going from managing zero points in the paint in the second quarter to scoring 16 in the third. Throw in a defensive effort that held the Phoenix without a basket for the first six-plus minutes of the period, and the Blue Devils were able to stretch out their margin to 49-37 at the 4:15 mark after layups from Jordan Wood and Nelson.

The Blue Devils would stretch that lead to 16 by late in the period on a three-point play by Wood, then didn't let the Phoenix get closer than seven again early in the fourth quarter.

Duke shot 45.3% from the field and finished with a 44-31 rebounding advantage that led to 19 second-chance points. The Blue Devils had four players reach double figures, including Texas transfer Aaliyah Crump going for 11 points, five rebounds and six assists in her Duke debut.

Maddy Skorupski finished with 16 points and six rebounds to lead Green Bay, while Kristina Ouimette added 14. But the Phoenix struggled after halftime, shooting just 6 of 27 (22.2%) while hanging around largely by making 12 of 14 free throws in the third quarter to carry the second-half offensive load.

Green Bay: Loyola Chicago visits the Phoenix in Saturday's home opener. Duke: The Blue Devils face North Texas on Sunday in San Antonio.

articles.title: UK's biggest TikTok creator Kyle Thomas to co-host BBC Naturewatch
articles.summary: Naturewatch, hosted by Chris Packham, Megan McCubbin and Kyle Thomas, is being made in Bristol.
articles.body:
The UK's most followed TikTok creator says he is "super excited" to be co-hosting the BBC's latest nature programme.

Naturewatch, hosted by wildlife presenters Chris Packham, Megan McCubbin and influencer Kyle Thomas, starts on Friday on BBC Two and will run all year round.

The show, which is being produced by BBC Studios' Natural History Unit, is filmed in a secret location just south of Bristol city centre, and will celebrate the best of British nature.

Thomas, who has amassed more than 33 million followers on TikTok for his videos about animals, said Naturewatch would act as a "trusted source of really brilliant factual information" as AI becomes increasingly common on social media.

He hopes his presence on the programme will attract a younger audience.

"We're going on this learning journey together," he said, adding: "I'm super, super excited. I'm learning so much already."

He explained the show would make nature accessible to everyone, with people encouraged to send videos in for the presenters to react to.

"It's really great to be in this part of the country, there's lots of brilliant wildlife here and lots of stories for us to be talking about," she added.

The programme will showcase the wildlife "people can expect to see and encounter whilst they're outside", said Packham.

articles.title: Nelly Korda wins LPGA Tour player-of-the-year award
articles.summary: World number one Nelly Korda claims her second points-based LPGA player-of-the-year award.
articles.body:
World number one Nelly Korda has claimed her second points-based LPGA player-of-the-year award.

The 28-year-old won four times this year, including the first two majors - The Chevron Championship and the US Women's Open at Riviera.

The American, who won the award in 2024, is one victory away from qualifying for the LPGA Hall of Fame.

To qualify for the Hall of Fame, a player must accumulate 27 points and meet a mandatory performance requirement.

A major championship win is worth two points, while an LPGA Tour victory is worth one point.

Asked about potentially entering the Hall of Fame, Korda, on 26 points, said in June: "I think it's an amazing accomplishment and it would be one of the best achievements of my career for sure."

The four-time major winner opened the 2026 LPGA Tour season with a six-tournament stretch where she either won or finished as the runner-up, to open a healthy lead in the points race.

South Korea's Haeran Ryu also won two majors this year but withdrew from last week's tournament in Malaysia because of injury.

And with Japan's Miyu Yamashita and Thailand's Jeeno Thitikul not entering The Annika next week in Florida, Korda secured the award with three tournaments remaining.

Korda would not be the youngest player to make the Hall of Fame as New Zealand's Lydia Ko and South Korea's Inbee Park were both 27 when they qualified.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy: World number two says LIV Golf wanted to 'destroy European Tour'
articles.summary: Six-time major winner Rory McIlroy says those connected to LIV Golf were expressing an ambition to "destroy the European Tour" at the 2026 Masters, only months before the league filed for bankruptcy protection.
articles.body:
Six-time major winner Rory McIlroy has said those connected to LIV Golf were expressing an ambition to "destroy the European Tour" at the 2026 Masters, only months before the league filed for bankruptcy protection.

The 37-year-old from Northern Ireland was a vocal opponent of LIV, the controversial Saudi-backed breakaway tour that attracted some of the biggest names in the sport when launched in 2022.

In an interview with the Scotsman , external this week, DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings said LIV had a stated aim to "destroy the DP World Tour" and McIlroy added that the claim was made at the Masters this year, a tournament he won at Augusta National for his second consecutive Green Jacket.

"I agree with everything that Guy said. They took players; they took sponsors; they turned professional golf into an arms race," said the world number two at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship

"They were going around Augusta saying they wanted to destroy the European Tour."

McIlroy continued: "It was always going to be good for a few years until something like this happened, or they realised they weren't going to get any return on investment, or they were going to leave the golf space and go invest in something else and invest in something that would actually make them money."

Westwood 'unemployed' amid LIV uncertainty as Rahm discusses exit

Garcia targets Ryder Cup return as he confirms LIV exit

Kimsey 'happy to trust tour' over safety in Abu Dhabi

'I think that there is going to be a bit of a reset'

With the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) having withdrawn its backing after previous investment of more than $5bn (£3.8bn), the league filed for bankruptcy protection last month.

While a possible $300m (£224m) in financing from BC Partners Credit could lead to what has been dubbed LIV 2.0, leading players including Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia have already walked away.

"I think we'll look back on it as a very strange time. It gave players a lot of leverage over the tours, and I don't necessarily think that's a good thing for the overall health of the professional game," said McIlroy.

"I do think there has to be a bit of a reset. They [LIV Golf] created a false economy within men's professional golf, and I think that there is going to be a bit of a reset here just for things to be a little bit more sustainable.

"There's not as much of an arms race as there was maybe a couple of years ago, and some players will argue that that's not good for players, but I think that's very short-term thinking. If you want sustainable tours, and we want these tours around in 50 years' time, there has to be sustainable business practices in place."

In Abu Dhabi this week McIlroy is seeking to bolster his bid to win the Race To Dubai for a record-equalling eighth time.

He goes into the penultimate event of the season at the Yas Links GC third in the standings behind leader Eugenio Chacarra and American Patrick Reed.

McIlroy trails Spaniard Chacarra by 999.03 points but his hopes of matching Colin Montgomerie's historic mark remain alive with 1,500 points on offer this week and a further 2,000 next week at the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.

"I'm excited to be here, excited to get going and excited to at least be in the conversation of trying to win another Race to Dubai," he said.

"I know I'm going to have to have a [good] week this week to do that. Hopefully I can and make things interesting going into next week.

"I think what gives me comfort is the amount of points that are on offer this week and next week. So even if I don't win but I still have a strong finish, I'll still feel like I have a realistic chance going into next week."

articles.title: Huntingdon train attack passengers thought stabbing was a 'joke'
articles.summary: The first person who was attacked also says he asked hospital staff "am I going to die today?".
articles.body:
Some train passengers initially remained sitting down and thought a man was joking after he told people "I've been stabbed, run", a court has heard.

Anthony Williams stabbed 10 people on the train which made an unscheduled stop in Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, on 1 November last year.

Cambridge Crown Court heard the first person who was stabbed, Jonathan Gjoshe, later asked hospital staff "am I going to die today?".

Williams, 33, of Langford Road in Peterborough, denies 10 counts of attempted murder, and four other alleged attempted murders in earlier incidents in Peterborough and London.

A second stabbing victim said Williams ran away when his pet cockapoo fought back, and another said he threw luggage at the attacker to fend him off.

Jurors have seen CCTV footage of Williams' attack , which took place on the York to London King's Cross LNER service, after it had left Peterborough.

The court was played a video interview with Gjoshe, who said he was on his phone in carriage J at the time and initially thought Williams was someone he knew.

"I've made eye contact with him… he's pulled a knife, but I just think it was the way he's poked me, the way he's stabbed me, it was a bit weird because it was slow."

Gjoshe said that once he felt a shock "that's when the adrenalin kicked in" and he jumped over the train table.

He said his whole arm was "drenched with blood" and went through the carriage telling people "I've been stabbed, run", but said some other people on the train remained "sitting down, thinking it was a joke".

"It was like a movie, it was quite horrific."

He spent four days in hospital and asked staff "am I going to die today or not? please tell me this".

Jurors then watched a video interview with another stabbing victim, Sachin Balakrishnan, who was a passenger in the same carriage.

He said he heard "screaming", then saw "people trying to jump over the seats" and running, then a man with a "big knife" who "was saying something but nothing meaningful".

Balakrishnan said he "ran and ran and ran", adding: "This guy was running behind me, there was nowhere to go. Nowhere was safe."

He said "everyone was running for their lives" and then he felt pain in his right arm.

The court also heard from David Presland, who said he was on his hands and knees on the floor when he was stabbed by Williams.

The 73-year-old said "I thought I was going to die" and "I'm lucky I survived."

Presland said another passenger called Kevin came to his aid.

Scott Green, who was travelling with his cockapoo Poppy in the next carriage along, said he initially thought there was a fight happening, before he "felt a jab" into his side.

In a recording of his interview, he said he fought back and told himself, "If I don't get this knife now I think he's going to kill me".

"I've tried to yank it... but I couldn't remove it," said Green.

He said his dog "went into attack mode" and startled the attacker, before Williams "done a runner".

Green described how a woman had "thrown him" to safety into a toilet, who subsequently joked: "I don't usually get in with men who I just met in the toilet".

He said the attacker was "just dead in the eyes, real dead... like he weren't there".

A fifth passenger, Kevin Deely, remembered shouting to Williams: "You don't have to do this, you don't have to do this."

In his recorded account, he described trying to shield a woman and throwing a piece of luggage at the assailant.

"It started to dawn on me I've been stabbed but I've no recollection of the event itself," Deely recalled.

He said his head was bleeding and others "started passing clothing back to us" to stem the bleeding.

"I remember feeling I was going to die there," he remembered.

Williams is also accused of attempting to murder Raza Aslam, Scott Bletcher, Stephen Crean, Kevin Deely, Michael Paffett, and Samir Zitouni on the London-bound train between Peterborough and Huntingdon on 1 November.

Prosecutors further allege that on 31 October, Williams tried to kill three people in Peterborough, before attempting to murder a teenager in the early hours of 1 November on a DLR train in east London.

Whether Williams carried out the attacks is not in question - the court has been told - but jurors must consider whether he intended to kill.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy calls for 'bit of a reset' in men's golf after claims LIV Golf wanted to 'destroy' DP World Tour
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy hopes men's golf can now have a reset after LIV Golf's attempts to "destroy" the DP World Tour; McIlroy was speaking ahead of the Abu Dhabi Albar Championship, live on Sky Sports Golf from Thursday
articles.body:
McIlroy successfully defended his Green Jacket at Augusta National in April, less than three weeks before Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) confirmed it would end funding for LIV Golf at the end of the season.

LIV Golf has since acquired new investment as they look to relaunch in 2027, despite many high-profile players - including Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton and Sergio Garcia - confirming they wouldn't re-sign with the league and would return to the DP World Tour.

DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings told The Scotsman last week that LIV Golf looked to 'destroy' the European circuit, having targeted DP World Tour events and sponsors, with McIlroy backing those suggestions and questioning the rival circuit.

"I agree with everything that Guy [Kinnings] said," McIlroy admitted ahead of the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, live on Sky Sports . "They [LIV Golf] took players; they took sponsors; they turned professional golf into an arms race.

"They were going around Augusta saying they wanted to destroy The European Tour (DP World Tour). Yeah, I agree with everything. I think people that don't agree are probably very short-sighted.

"There was some of the money that they used the right way, created the International Series on the Asian Tour, great for a couple years, but where did that leave the Asian Tour? They left them high and dry.

"Asian Tour came back into the fold, did a partnership with the PGA Tour and the European Tour - again, this was always going to be the case.

"It was always going to be good for a few years until something like this happened, or they realised they weren't going to get any return on investment, or they were going to leave the golf space and go invest in something else and invest in something that would actually make them money.

"I think for long-term sustainability for men's professional golf, I think we are in a much better spot."

Sky Sports reached out to LIV Golf for comment over Kinnings' claims, since reiterated by McIlroy.

Rahm said on Tuesday he left LIV Golf because he "wasn't willing to follow" the path that the new iteration of the circuit was taking, with McIlroy hoping that the men's game can now stabilise after a turbulent few years.

"We'll look back on it as a very strange time," McIlroy added. "It gave players a lot of leverage over the tours and I don't necessarily think that's a good thing for the overall health of the professional game.

"They created a false economy within men's professional golf, and I think that there is going to be a bit of a reset here - just for things to be a little bit more sustainable. There's not as much of an arms race as there was maybe a couple of years ago.

"Some players will argue that that's not good for players, but I think that's very short-term thinking. If you want sustainable tours, and we want these tours around in 50 years' time, there has to be sustainable business practises in place to make sure they are around in 50 years' time."

articles.title: Women's TGL: Sky Sports to show exclusive live coverage of new women's team golf league featuring LPGA Tour stars
articles.summary: Charley Hull and Lottie Woad are among the LPGA Tour stars involved in the inaugural women's TGL season; every match of the WTGL is live on Sky Sports, featuring five teams, with the season launching on November 8
articles.body:

articles.title: Rajasthan bans dusty construction, limits firecrackers in NCR districts around Diwali
articles.summary: Rajasthan bans dust-generating construction in NCR districts Nov 5–20 and allows only CSIR-NEERI certified green crackers Nov 7–8 in limited hours.
articles.body: Jaipur: The Rajasthan govt has prohibited dust-generating construction and demolition activities in its National Capital Region (NCR) districts from Nov 5 to 20 to control air pollution. It has also restricted the use of firecrackers in five NCR districts, allowing only certified green crackers on Nov 7 and 8 during specified hours.Chief Secretary V Srinivas directed departments to ensure strict compliance with the restrictions while reviewing air pollution control measures in the state’s NCR region at a meeting Wednesday.A senior govt official said, “As per the directions issued in compliance with a Supreme Court order, only green crackers certified by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) will be permitted in Alwar, Bharatpur, Deeg, Khairthal-Tijara and Kotputli-Behror districts.”Green crackers can be burst only from 6 am to 7 am and 8 pm to 10 pm on Nov 7 and 8, with their use outside these time slots prohibited.Hospitals, nursing homes, primary and district health centres, old-age homes and educational institutions have been declared silent and no-cracker zones, and firecrackers will not be permitted within 300 metres of these establishments.The meeting was informed that, following directions of Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), dust-generating demolition and open construction activities would remain prohibited in the NCR districts from Nov 5 to 20.“Exemptions have been provided for specified projects related to railways, metro services, airports, interstate bus terminals, hospitals, water supply, sanitation, national security and projects of national importance,” the govt official added. The restrictions will also cover highways, roads, flyovers, overbridges, power transmission lines, pipelines and telecommunications projects.Srinivas directed departments to regularly monitor construction and demolition waste management through a dashboard. He asked officials to maximise the use of mechanised road-sweeping machines and operate them in two shifts to control road dust. articles.title: Tributes paid to drummer Clem Cattini who has died aged 89
articles.summary: Amarillo singer Tony Christie says Clem Cattini was a "world class" musician and gentleman.
articles.body:
Tributes have been paid after the death of drummer Clem Cattini, who performed on several UK Number One singles.

The 89-year-old, who lived in Hertfordshire, co-founded the Tornados in 1961. Their instrumental Telstar spent five weeks at the top of the UK chart in 1962, and they became the first British group to top the US Billboard Hot 100.

As a session musician, he played on number one hits such as Tom Jones' Green, Green Grass of Home, Dusty Springfield's You Don't Have To Say You Love Me and Tony Christie's (Is This the Way to) Amarillo?.

In a Facebook post Christie described Cattini as "a world class musician but also a world class gentleman".

He wrote: "So very sad to hear that the great Clem Cattini, drummer of the Tornados and prolific session drummer has passed away. Clem played on more number 1 records than any other British drummer.

"Proud to have known him. My condolences and love to his family."

Carl Palmer, drummer with groups Emerson, Lake & Palmer and Asia, said: "The drummers all over the UK owe you a lot for opening the door for all of us."

North London band The Equals, who topped the charts in 1968 with Baby Come Back, posted on social media : "The legendary Clem Cattini, a true powerhouse of percussion and one of the most prolific drummers in British recording history.

"An absolute legend who leaves behind an incredible musical legacy."

Cattini also played on Engelbert Humperdinck's Release Me, Love Affair's Everlasting Love and Johnny Kidd & The Pirates' Shakin' All Over.

Teen musician is flying the flag for the recorder

His other credits included recording with Paul Weller, The Kinks and The Wombles.

He played drums on all 11 tracks of Thrillington, an instrumental reworking of Paul and Linda McCartney's album Ram, which the former Beatle released under the pseudonym Percy "Thrills" Thrillington.

Cattini toured with Cliff Richard and Roy Orbison, and performed on television with the Top Of the Pops orchestra.

He was played by James Corden in the 2008 film Telstar, about Tornados producer Joe Meek.

articles.title: LIV Golf: Breakaway league to wind down after potential financial backers withdraw support
articles.summary: LIV Golf is set to announce on Thursday it will wind down after a financing firm retracted its support.
articles.body:
LIV Golf is set to be wound down after its investor withdrew support because the proposed new league failed to attract enough players.

LIV had hoped BC Partners Credit would provide a possible $300m (£223m) in financing after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) withdrew its backing in April , leading to the league filing for bankruptcy protection in September.

The funding could have helped the competition move forward in a new form, dubbed LIV 2.0, but BC Partners is understood to have decided it is not viable to pursue a deal.

While leading players such as Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia had already walked away, BBC Sport understands that those working on LIV 2.0 had received commitments from co-investors, felt support from within the golf ecosystem and had about 30 players signed up, including major winners.

But sources say the timelines ultimately proved insurmountable and they could not get the agreements they needed to move forward.

The league had been facing a deadline to show it had enough player support to continue in 2027.

The expectation is that an attorney acting for LIV will announce in a court hearing on Thursday that the proposal for LIV 2.0 is not viable.

LIV aimed to 'destroy the European Tour' - McIlroy

Westwood 'unemployed' amid LIV uncertainty as Rahm discusses exit

What next for LIV Golf's star players, and its fight for survival?

LIV Golf has provided one of the most tumultuous episodes in the history of golf since its launch in 2021, one which threatened to tear the sport apart.

High-profile players joined and were banned from other tours, as well as events such as the Ryder Cup.

More than $5bn (£3.7bn) was spent by PIF, with major winners including Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau lured by lucrative contracts and vast prize money.

But the future of the concept - and its star players - has been shrouded in uncertainty this year after the 2026 season ended early. An event in August in Indianapolis proved to be the last.

When PIF announced it was withdrawing its funding in April, LIV announced a "strategic evolution" - including a newly established independent board - and attempted to find replacement financial investors.

The exodus of players continued, however, including the exits of Rahm, Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton and Graeme McDowell. When Rahm left it was reported he was owed about $100m (£75m) from the remainder of the contract.

The European tour, which is sponsored by DP World, had also increased pressure on players when it announced last month that those who signed up to LIV Golf next season would not be allowed to be members of the European tour in 2027.

That would have also spelled an end to any players with ambitions of featuring in the Ryder Cup as only DP World Tour members can play for Europe in the biennial team competition.

Speaking this week, Lee Westwood, one of the most high-profile players to join LIV when it first began in 2022, said the proposed revamp still had potential to thrive but added "there hasn't been anything presented to me that is agreeable for LIV 2.0".

DeChambeau, who had not revealed his future plans, said he hopes the league "exists forever", while former Taylor Made and Adidas executive Mark King was appointed as a senior adviser last week.

A loose deadline for LIV to confirm its players for 2027 had been set for last Sunday - a point which, having now passed, appears to be drawing the saga to an end.

articles.title: Report: LIV's Financial Backer Dropping Plan for New League in 2027
articles.summary: LIV Golf's main investor to help it emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy is scrapping plans for a new version because it lacked enough player support, The Financial Times reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
LIV Golf's main investor to help it emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy is scrapping plans for a new version because it lacked enough player support, The Financial Times reported Wednesday.

BC Partners Credit had pledged as much as $300 million for what was called "LIV 2.0," which was planning at least 10 tournaments, an emphasis on teams and equity for players. LIV CEO Scott O'Neil had called the equity a "second bite of the apple."

But that required enough players to sign up for LIV 2.0. Four players, including Brendan Steele and Cameron Tringale, publicly stated their support. LIV was believed to have as many as 30 players who were willing to stay with the league, but it was lacking the star power.

Ted Goldthorpe, partner and head of BC Partners Credit, said at a Sportico conference in September, "A lot of the money that was spent created the ecosystem and infrastructure that exists today. We think we can run this in a financially sustainable way because much of that spending went to getting the players, and the players are here."

Jon Rahm was released from his contract in a deal that was to be approved at a hearing Thursday in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in New Jersey. Now, the Financial Times reported that hearing would shift toward LIV seeking liquidation of its assets.

LIV Golf officials did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

LIV Golf New Jersey filed for a change of address in the bankruptcy court on Wednesday, from an office in New York to Claymont, Delaware, a commercial office property.

The Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia was behind LIV Golf when it launched in 2022 by luring away several big names — Dustin Johnson, Brooks Koepka, Bryson DeChambeau and eventually Rahm — with signing bonuses of nine figures.

Even run-of-the mill players with only one PGA Tour victory signed for $30 million, more than they had earned in their career.

The league, originally run by Greg Norman, spent more than $5 billion. But a few months after the start of the Iran war, PIF changed its investment strategy in April and said it would no longer pay for LIV Golf after the 2026 season.

The Asian Tour, which received a financial boost from LIV for an International Series, decided in July to renew an alliance with the PGA Tour and European tour.

And as LIV was trying to emerge from bankruptcy, filed on Sept. 8, the European tour laid down a crushing ultimatum by saying anyone who signed with LIV 2.0 need not apply for membership in the commercially known DP World Tour.

That would make European players ineligible for the Ryder Cup.

Guy Kinnings, the European tour CEO, called out LIV in an interview with The Scotsman when he said, "But we also have to protect the tour against an entity who spent, so we are told, over $7 billion, with one of their aims being to 'destroy the DP World Tour.'"

Rahm, Sergio Garcia, Louis Oosthuizen and Tyrrell Hatton also said they would no longer stay with LIV, and the rival league also lost young players like David Puig of Spain and Tom McKibbin of Northern Ireland.

The year began with Brooks Koepka getting out of his LIV deal with one year remaining, and the PGA Tour created a path — with financial penalties — to return. Patrick Reed chose not to extend his deal and now is poised to return to the PGA Tour next year through his performance in Europe.

Rahm had said on Tuesday he would be willing to pay the same price as Koepka, though it was unlikely that same deal would be offered.

LIV 2.0 was pushing player equity and prize money that was more than half of the $20 million purses for individuals when it began in 2022. LIV's final event was in August in Indianapolis, won by Michael La Sasso. He failed to get through the second stage of European tour Q-school last week.

articles.title: El LIV Golf 2.0. está casi descartado y a punto de la desaparición
articles.standfirst: La negativa de las estrellas a apoyar el circuito lleva al fondo de inversión BC Partners a retirar la oferta de 300 millones para seguir
articles.summary: La negativa de las estrellas a apoyar el circuito lleva al fondo de inversión BC Partners a retirar la oferta de 300 millones para seguir
articles.body: El LIV Golf 2.0. se ha apagado antes de empezar. Según revela 'Financial Times', la segunda vista de la bancarrota declarada tras la retirada de la financiación al circuito del Fondo Público de Arabia Saudí (PIF) se producirá este jueves y ahí se conocerá la retirada de la oferta del fondo de inversión BC Partners, que había anunciado un montante de 300 millones de dólares para que saliese adelante. El objetivo de BC Partners era apoyar una liga, sobre todo, porque el resto de sus activos deportivos podrían acogerse a un mejor sistema impositivo debido a adquirir un producto, la herencia del LIV genuino, con unas pérdidas operativas de 5.400 millones de dólares, pero ni siquiera eso ha sido suficiente. El continuo rechazo de golfistas a ese proyecto, incluido Bryson DeChambeau que parecía el primer interesado, ha condenado a la situación actual. La realidad es que públicamente jugadores como Jon Rahm, Sergio García, Tyrrell Hatton, Graeme McDowell, Louis Oosthuizen, David Puig y Tom McKibbin han hecho pública su salida, incluso Lee Westwood, y, en cambio, sólo cuatro jugadores de los que no mueven la aguja, Ben Campbell, Cameron Tringale, Richard Bland y Brendan Steele, han manifestado su deseo de seguir. La idea expuesta por su CEO, Scott O'Neil, era llevar a cabo una temporada con 10 torneos y explotar el concepto de equipos nacionales, sobre todo por el impulso de Sudáfrica y Australia. Calculaban que 30 jugadores permanecerían, pero el resultado ha sido nefasto y no se puede sostener con un cartel de segunda fila. Para colmo, el DP World Tour, el circuito europeo de toda la vida, que podría haber sido un perfecto aliado para dar calendario a los jugadores que permaneciesen anunció que quien firmase por el LIV 2.0. no tendría cabida en sus torneos y se cerraría la puerta de la Ryder Cup. Fue la estocada definitiva. Incluso su director general Guy Kinnings explicó en una entrevista en 'The Scotsman', que el propósito que le había manifestado el LIV en abril, justo la semana antes de anunciar Arabia Saudí su espantada, era que querían "destruir el DP World Tour". Fuentes del LIV Golf han desmentido esto. Sin la alianza con el Asian Tour, ahora bajo el abrigo del PGA Tour, las opciones se han agotado. Se asiste, por lo tanto, a lo que parece la muerte definitiva del LIV Golf. Un proyecto que nació hace cinco temporadas con la idea de convertirse en la alternativa al circuito americano, que pretendía llevar al golf a otra dimensión y que ha terminado adeudando dinero a varias de sus estrellas, entre ellas Jon Rahm, que podría haber dejado de percibir casi 100 millones de dólares de los prometidos en su millonario contrato. De hecho, el PIF podría sólo haber aportado este último año 200 millones de los 500 necesarios para cerrar el curso. El Financial Times añade que la audiencia judicial prevista para el jueves en el tribunal de quiebras pasaría a centrarse en que LIV pida la liquidación de sus activos. Todo apunta a un desmantelamiento ordenado, no a un renacimiento. La retirada generalizada del apoyo a todos los activos deportivos fuera de sus fronteras de Arabia Saudi (e incluso dentro) arroja su principal cadáver.

articles.title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 match predictions, expert picks for every matchup in Riyadh
articles.summary: Here's a breakdown of all the action and predictions for who will win at the latest Crown Jewel event.
articles.body:
WWE returns to Saudi Arabia for the latest Crown Jewel event. The event will feature title bouts, with WWE's marquee players competing for bragging rights.

Two WWE Crown Jewel Championship belts are on the line. Champions from Raw and SmackDown face off for more gold. Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn, Liv Morgan, and Chelsea Green all have something to prove.

Meanwhile, a rivalry looks to be settled when Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton compete in a Last Man Standing match. The tag team titles are also on the line.

Here's a breakdown of all the action and predictions for who will win at the latest Crown Jewel event.

Roman Reigns (Raw Champion) vs. Sami Zayn (SmackDown Champion) for the WWE Crown Jewel Championship

Reigns and Zayn renew their story from a few years ago. This time, Zayn is a champion.

Reigns has put on great performances in 2026, but he's been preoccupied with the 946 group. Zayn has enemies left and right as champion, but Reigns and The Bloodline have had a tough time with Royce Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Prince, Carmelo Hayes, Jaida Parker, and now Cruz Montana.

There's no doubt Reigns and Zayn will have a good match that starts slow and ends with a bang. However, expect interference at the highest level, from 946 and The Bloodline. Zayn will take advantage of all the chaos and sneak in a win.

Liv Morgan (Raw Champion) vs. Chelsea Green (SmackDown Champion) for the WWE Crown Jewel Championship

Chelsea Green has proven to be a fighting champion since getting the interim tag off her reign. She has had to keep an eye on friend and Money in the Bank winner Tiffany Stratton. Liv Morgan, a previous Crown Jewel Champion, has been untouchable with The Judgment Day in her corner.

The story of Stratton holding the briefcase is almost too similar to her 2024 run with it. Given that, WWE could potentially give fans a shocking twist. Stratton could cash in on Green after Morgan beats her, potentially thanks to Stratton stabbing her friend in the back.

Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing match

Rhodes retained the Undisputed WWE Championship against Orton at WrestleMania 42 in a match that featured Pat McAfee. While it wasn't well received, the end, Orton punting Rhodes unconscious, was. Now, months later, the two are feuding again.

This time, Rhodes must punt Orton in the head.

Rhodes almost did it at Sunday Night's Main Event but hesitated. He did it to Baron Corbin. The story of Orton getting his comeuppance has been building for a while. Rhodes will hesitate before executing, leading to one big crescendo of a finish. It's the only way the match should end.

The Vision (Bron Breakker and Austin Theory) (c) vs. Penta and Je'Von Evans for the World Tag Team Championship

Bron Breakker has regained momentum, with and without The Vision's help. Put into the tag team scene following Logan Paul's injury, Breakker has made it clear he's ready for bigger things. In this case, dropping the titles makes sense.

Je'Von Evans is dynamic, and Penta is a true favorite. Normally, momentum is lost while holding the Money in the Bank briefcase. However, in this case, Penta should have a rocket put on his back.

Breakker should move on to the world title picture after this match. The only way to continue his momentum is to lose a match and let the red-hot high flyers win.

Sporting News prediction: Penta and Je'Von Evans
